| | For too long, unelected elites have chipped away at the rule of American citizens--replacing self-government with open borders and control by a ruling class unaccountable to the people.

As someone who loves this country, I know that weighs on you--it troubles me too. That's why this course matters.

**Victor Davis Hanson **traces the history of citizenship from ancient Greece and Rome to the American founding--and shows how we can restore it before it's lost.

In eight fascinating lectures, you'll explore:

* The erosion of the middle class and self-rule
* The disappearance of sovereign borders
* The rise of tribalism and the "deep state"
* Modern assaults on the Constitution and freedom

This course will open your eyes to the challenges we face--and inspire you to help defend liberty.

Peter,
In unity there is strength, and over the course of this month, the world has seen and been inspired by this very strength in Minnesota.
Minneapolis residents of all walks of life have come together and are showing us what solidarity in action looks like, as they bravely resist a federal occupation of their city amid state violence and killings.
Solidarity is a core value at TOP, and with our nation in peril, we know it's unshakeable solidarity that will help get us out of this dire time and bring brighter days. We also understand fully that while it's Minnesota today, this regime could target any one of our cities and states in the coming months. This is what makes our collective support of Minnesota all the more powerful.
Donate now to community groups providing needed assistance to people whose lives have been uprooted by this hostile occupation – from mutual aid to on-the-ground services. [https://www.standwithminnesota.com/]
https://www.standwithminnesota.com/ [https://www.standwithminnesota.com/]
Sustaining and growing people-powered movements requires us all stepping up to the plate to assist fellow community members in the ways we can. This is how we make lasting change that’s seen and felt by ALL.
Make a contribution today to community groups offering mutual aid and other services to directly-impacted Minnesotans. [https://www.standwithminnesota.com/]
Together, let’s show these courageous residents we have their backs.
We appreciate you,

**I’m not exactly your typical politician.** I used to work as a scientist — a geologist to be specific. After our company was sold and I got laid off, I organized and opened Colorado’s first brewpub, helping revitalize a neglected warehouse district in Denver.
I found my way to public office because I was fed up with everyday Coloradans’ voices being drowned out by special interests and corporations. My friends and I felt like our elected officials were mainly making decisions to get re-elected, not solve problems for their constituents. I ran for mayor, then governor, and eventually senator, always focusing on the same thing: putting Colorado families first and getting sh*t done.
I’m proud of the work we’ve accomplished together in the Senate — from lowering prescription drug costs, to defending our public lands, to standing up against Trump’s disastrous agenda.
**But just over a year into Trump’s second term, Colorado has faced nonstop attacks from the President — and it’s clear there are still plenty more important fights ahead of us.**
Trump has weaponized the federal government against us for refusing to bend to his will. He announced plans to dismantle the National Center for Atmospheric Research (NCAR) in Boulder, and threatened to rip away child care resources from our state and nation. The President actually vetoed a bipartisan bill passed by unanimous consent in both chambers of Congress that, for the first time, would bring clean drinking water to 50,000 rural Coloradans. This is the first time such a unanimously passed bill has been vetoed by the president since President Johnson. No, not Lyndon Johnson! _I’m talking about Andrew Johnson 150 years ago._
It’s hard to overstate the unprecedented threat working people and our democracy are facing under this administration — and it’s so important that we do everything we can to push back on Trump and his dangerous agenda.
**Taking back the Senate this November is a key part of that fight,_and that work starts with defending this must-hold seat in Colorado._**

Friend, The Senate will vote this week on whether to send $65 billion more U.S. taxpayer dollars to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS)—which includes ICE and Border Patrol. This weekend, **immigration agents killed another person in Minneapolis.** **A VA nurse, Alex Pretti** came to help a woman who’d been hurt by the agents. His last words were, “Are you OK?” After that, Border Patrol agents surrounded him, tear-gassed him and tackled him to the ground, beat him, then shot him 10 times—executing him in the street. They’re concerned about staying on track to our $500,000 January online fundraising goal — but I _know_ that this team always steps up. **[Even so, I do have to ask: Can you pitch in right away to help close the gap to our goal? Only if it fits in your budget.](https://act.roycooper.com/go/5177?t=8&akid=430%2E124072%2Efwwb01)** Thanks so much, Roy [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/5177?t=9&akid=430%2E124072%2Efwwb01)

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

name: Mark Ronchetti
subject: "They're Not Law Enforcement"
body:
Plus: NM's DA threatens to arrest ICE agents | And, the top animal you SHOULD be afraid of | New for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=b0389fcf73&e=567664f14c)
| | | | | |
Tim Walz just said the quiet part out loud.
After an armed man was shot dead confronting ICE agents in Minneapolis, the governor of Minnesota stood in front of cameras and told America: ["Stop referring to these people as law enforcement. They're not law enforcement."](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=a71657ccc2&e=567664f14c)
Meanwhile, Chicago's police chief gave his city the exact opposite message. Same week. Same party. We play both clips — and the contrast will make your blood boil.
---
[|
---](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=e5ca432d0f&e=567664f14c)
| |
**💀 WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED IN MINNEAPOLIS**
They're not telling you the full story. The man who was killed showed up armed with a concealed weapon and dozens of rounds of ammunition. He physically blocked a federal operation. He wrestled with agents.
We walk through the footage — and show you exactly what Walz said in response.

**🔥 TWO LEADERS. TWO MESSAGES.**
Chicago's police chief — in a blue city — told his residents:
"Do NOT box in law enforcement officers. You are breaking the law and putting yourself in danger."
Tim Walz told Minnesota the opposite. We play both clips back to back so you can see the difference in leadership.
---
| [Stream Episode Now](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=e64834e870&e=567664f14c)
---
| |
**🎭 SAM BREGMAN PROVES THIS ISN'T JUST MINNESOTA**
New Mexico's DA went on CNN threatening to arrest ICE agents. His claims about agents "pulling over Hispanics to check citizenship" have zero evidence behind them.
It's the same playbook — and he's running for Governor. We expose exactly what's happening.
---
| [Stream Episode Now](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=2faf45434b&e=567664f14c)
---
| |
**💰 THE BILL THAT COULD COLLAPSE NEW MEXICO'S ECONOMY**
Senate Bill 18 wants New Mexico to hit net zero by 2050. Europe tried this — $500 billion invested, 20% less electricity, prices tripled.
We explain what this means for your electric bill and the schools funded by oil and gas revenue.
**📊 SNAP ERROR RATES HIT 16%**
New Mexico has the highest SNAP rate in America. We also have the 5th worst error rate nationally — and it just tripled since 2014.
The feds are about to make us pay for it.

**🐝 THE ANIMAL MOST LIKELY TO KILL YOU**
Mark put Krysty on the spot with a quiz about the deadliest animals in America. Spoiler: it's not the mountain lions she's terrified of from the game camera footage.
The actual answer? You'll never guess. (Hint: Krysty was NOT happy about it.)

After an armed man was shot dead confronting ICE agents in Minneapolis, the governor of Minnesota stood in front of cameras and told America: Meanwhile, Chicago's police chief gave his city the exact opposite message. The man who was killed showed up armed with a concealed weapon and dozens of rounds of ammunition. He physically blocked a federal operation. He wrestled with agents. We walk through the footage — and show you exactly what Walz said in response. 🔥 TWO LEADERS. TWO MESSAGES. Chicago's police chief — in a blue city — told his residents: "Do NOT box in law enforcement officers. You are breaking the law and putting yourself in danger." Tim Walz told Minnesota the opposite. clean_body: They only need a handful to flip control of Congress, and they’re building their entire strategy around that reality. | Fellow American — I want to be completely candid with you about what we’re walking into this year. The 2026 midterms are not routine — they’re shaping up to be a referendum election, and Democrats are already operating like they can taste the Speaker’s gavel again. Republicans hold the House right now, but our majority is razor-thin, and we cannot afford even a small slip in turnout, enthusiasm, or resources. The hard truth is Democrats don’t need a “wave.” They don’t need 30 seats. They only need a handful to flip control of Congress, and they’re building their entire strategy around that reality. They’re targeting competitive districts nationwide, recruiting challengers, and using every headline they can to fuel small-dollar fundraising and motivate their base. And we all know what happens if Democrats take the House. Deporting criminal illegal aliens is shutdown. We’ll be fighting tax increases instead of delivering tax cuts. And crazy Leftists will run all the committees. Instead of results, Washington becomes a circus again — investigations, subpoenas, political stunts, and endless obstruction designed to paralyze President Trump’s final two years in office. If Democrats flip the House, the America First agenda is dead on arrival. That’s why I’m reaching out today. We have a narrow window to build the resources we need early so we can define this race on our terms, win the air war, and fund a serious turnout operation before Democrats’ outside money starts flooding in. We’ve worked too hard to let the radical left claw their way back into power and turn Congress into an emergency brake on President Trump’s agenda, fellow American. body:
Patrick wants to make the government work for everyone, not just the powerful and wealthy.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260127-1&t=1&akid=3090%2E587540%2EQA8oNu)
We have exciting news, Peter.
**Leaders We Deserve is proud to announce that we are endorsing our newest incumbent challenger: Patrick Roath for US Congress in Massachusetts’ 8th Congressional District!**
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260127_1_roath.RIfBRO&refcode=em20260127-3090&t=2&akid=3090%2E587540%2EQA8oNu)
Patrick is running because he believes democracy _should_ work, and that the government should once again be in the business of helping create the American Dream for everyone, not just those with power and money.
**[If you’re ready to elect leaders who will defend democracy and actually deliver results, will you split a $5 contribution between Patrick’s campaign and Leaders We Deserve today?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260127_1_roath.RIfBRO&refcode=em20260127-3090&amount=5&t=3&akid=3090%2E587540%2EQA8oNu)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260127_1_roath.RIfBRO&amount=5&refcode=em20260127-3090&t=22&akid=3090%2E587540%2EQA8oNu)**
Here’s why we’re backing Patrick, Peter:
**He’s a fighter for democracy, and has the record to prove it.** As a voting rights attorney and former Chair of Common Cause Massachusetts, Patrick helped secure wins for automatic voter registration, mail-in voting, and ballot access during the pandemic when democracy itself was under threat. Patrick has taken on powerful institutions — _and won —_ to make sure people can vote and be heard. Patrick’s commitment and experience in protecting democracy is exactly what we need more of at this time of crisis in democracy in our country.
This district is ready for new leadership, Peter. Patrick’s opponent, Stephen Lynch, has been in office for more than **_two decades_** , and voters are increasingly frustrated that he’s not listening or adapting as the district changes.
As a state legislator, Lynch supported a gay panic defense legislation that would have allowed someone accused of assaulting a gay person to argue that the victim’s identity or behavior provoked the attack. He also voted against an assault weapons ban and dismissed it as “feel-good legislation.” In Congress, Lynch was the _only_ Democrat from New England to vote _against_ the Affordable Care Act, and he’s the _last_ Democrat left in Congress who voted against the law in 2010. And last summer, while Trump was deploying the US military to Los Angeles to crush peaceful anti-ICE protests, Stephen Lynch voted to “express gratitude” for ICE. More recently, he’s the _only_ Democrat from Massachusetts who backed the Laken Riley Act, which expanded deportation authority based on accusations alone.
His constituents want him out, too — and they’re calling him out on his B.S. During a speech he held outside of a local VA last February, Lynch was quick to dismiss his constituents when they expressed their disappointment at him not pushing back against Trump and his agenda. He even told a voter that if they wanted to decide what was best for the district, _they_ should run for Congress and made it clear that the decisions that are made for MA-08 are only for HIM to decide.
It’s clear that he’s completely disconnected from the people he represents, and it’s _crazy_ to believe that this is what so many people in the Democratic establishment are trying to defend.
**That’s why we’re supporting Patrick. He’s a clear contrast to Stephen; principled, prepared, and focused on delivering results — not defending outdated positions for political comfort.**
We believe Patrick can win this race. But he’s going to need a lot of support.
**[So if you’re with us in backing the next generation of leaders who will defend democracy, expand opportunity, and actually get things done, will you split a $5 donation between Patrick’s campaign and Leaders We Deserve today?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260127_1_roath.RIfBRO&refcode=em20260127-3090&amount=5&t=23&akid=3090%2E587540%2EQA8oNu)**
Thank you for your support,
Leaders We Deserve

body:
Peter, I want to follow up on our efforts to support Minnesota leaders targeted by the Trump Administration.
Mayor Jacob Frey of Minneapolis is facing an investigation for speaking out and insisting on accountability for the violent occupation of his city by the federal government. And the reason ICE is in Minneapolis is because Donald Trump wants them there. ICE wears masks and uses deadly force because they are obeying Donald Trump.
I am enraged and heartbroken for Alex Pretti and Renee Good, for their families, for Minneapolis, and for America.
America watched Donald Trump react to these tragedies in real time and blame the victims. Investigation blocked. No patience. No compassion.
A full and fair investigation at the state level is absolutely necessary. We cannot stand for the pure gaslighting — especially from the President of the United States.
So when Donald Trump launched a politically motivated investigation into Mayor Frey for protecting his community, I knew I had to rally together this team to respond.

In each of these 26 states, the results from these Secretary of State elections will determine not just who holds those offices but how future elections are run and the shape of our democracy as a whole.
We must make sure that pro-voter, pro-democracy, anti-suppression candidates win everywhere we can. RUSH $35 or more right now to give us the resources we need to push all year to register and turn out every eligible voter >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=012726_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
These types of elections always fly under the media's radar, Team, but this year 26 Secretary of State races will shape the future of our elections, redistricting in 2030, and the outcome of the 2028 presidential race.
Opponents of voting rights already know this, which is why they’re already pouring money into these elections – and we have to fight back now, while it still makes a difference. Check out this map:
Map of Key Secretary of State Races for 2026 [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=012726_3&amount=25]
The work to increase voter participation and turnout for these races has to start now, not this summer. We have to build the infrastructure to defend pro-voter initiatives in Arizona, Michigan, Wisconsin, and Nevada, at the same time as we work to flip the script in key battleground states like Georgia, Ohio, and Iowa.

Opponents of voting rights have been working on these objectives for years. They've targeted state legislatures and key statewide offices to control the rules around voting and that's why they've been in a position to follow up on the "Big Lie" with bill after bill suppressing the vote. They've played the long game to pick and choose their voters and protect their own power.
Most people don't know that their Secretary of State is the state official who runs their elections, let alone who the current office-holder in their state is. But they are the last line of defense against voter suppression and diminished ballot access , which is why we need to invest in voter information, registration, and participation in these critical races.
2025 was a tough year, but we did not back down. Our right to vote is too important and too much is at stake for our democracy, our fellow Americans, and the direction of our country. Driving pro-voting rights voters to the polls in November is the best possible response to all that we've been forced to live through the last decade.
Your gift -- $10, $20, $35, or more -- helps provide the resources we need to keep voters apprised of what is at stake and get them out to vote for pro-democracy policies. Please, chip in what you can today! >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=012726_3&amount=35]

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

subject: My heart is heavy
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:

---
Friend, my heart is heavy.

On Saturday, while Minnesotans and many across the country stood against the disgusting and terrifying violence ICE is carrying out in our country, federal agents shot and killed another person. He was not the first person unjustly killed by ICE, and most likely, he will not be the last, and I know that’s why so many people are angry. I’m angry too.

I don't have the words to express my horror at what is happening in our country right now, but I do know that we must continue to fight back — in any way we can. Resistance can be organizing a protest, delivering coffee and providing a warm place for protestors, or calling your lawmakers or running for local office. Hope is only lost when resistance stops, and there is power in our voices and collective action.
**New Mexicans are not strangers to adversity. In fact, we are strong and support each other. To New Mexicans who are living in fear, worrying about loved ones, and watching what is happening in our communities with horror, I want you to know I stand with you in this fight — I always have and I always will. Today, as your neighbor and friend. Next year, as your governor.
**
While state and local law enforcement work hard to protect our communities, under-trained ICE agents are using violence, rounding people up, tearing families apart, targeting Black and brown communities, and breaking the law. And now, Americans are being killed in the streets for standing up, speaking out, and opposing them.
**This is unacceptable. Our communities are _less safe_ as a direct result of Donald Trump's policies. It's un-American, and it must stop.**
If Donald Trump and ICE want to bring the violence and unrest to New Mexico, they will have to get through my administration and me. We will have zero tolerance for their injustice, and we will use every authority at our disposal to stop them.
I will do everything in my power to protect our public spaces — like schools, churches, courthouses, healthcare centers, and state government facilities.
I will support efforts to require ICE agents to identify themselves and remove their masks and to ban ICE detention centers in our state.
Governors are the last line of defense when the federal government abuses its resources and undermines civil liberties. Our responsibility is to protect families, safeguard our communities, and make sure no one lives in fear. You have my promise: I will hold Donald Trump accountable and protect New Mexicans. Always.
This isn't over. I expect it will get harder before it gets easier. But together, we will defend our rights and liberties.
With you in this fight,

Deb

The reality is that the same President who led a violent insurrection and called it a “peaceful protest” is now using his power to unleash brutality and violence against _actual_ peaceful protesters.
To see this kind of state violence is not only to witness the killing of a human being, but also the spiraling spiritual death of a nation. It is clear that we are losing our humanity.

Our country is better than this. We are better than this.
Today, I visited the memorial for Alex Pretti in Minneapolis and met with local faith leaders to pray for his loved ones, his community, and the soul of our country. But we all have to pray in this moment – not only with our lips, but also with our feet.

That's why, as a United States Senator, I plan to vote against funding for ICE this week and continue to use every tool at my disposal to hold immigration enforcement officials accountable. In this defining moment for our nation, you can count on me to fight with everything I have for justice and our fundamental freedoms as Americans. That is my promise to you – now and always.
Thank you for standing with me,

Rev. Raphael Warnock

In just a short time, I will address the nation.

[GET BEHIND TRUMP!](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)

**A major truth is about to come out.** **Something they never wanted exposed.** **Something that could change history.**
[GET BEHIND TRUMP!](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
But here’s the truth they don’t want you to hear:

The pressure on me right now is enormous. The attacks are relentless.

**And I cannot move forward unless I know the American people are standing with me.[Friend, are you STILL with me?>](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)**

Before I step up and speak - before this truth bomb drops - I need to hear from YOU.

**Not later.** **Not after the headlines.** **NOW.**

[STAND WITH TRUMP](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
Every month that passes, one thing becomes more crystal clear than ever:

America is coming back. The momentum is real. And Make America is no longer a promise – it’s happening.

**[Friend, before all eyes are on me, I need to know — are you still with me? Make it crystal clear here.>](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)**
Thank you,
President Donald J. Trump

disclaimer_text: Paid for by Maxine for Congress
body:
https://maxinefororegon.com/ [https://maxinefororegon.com/]
Exciting news, Peter.
I just filed for re-election in Oregon’s Third Congressional District.
There is no time to waste. The people of Oregon’s Third District deserve a representative who doesn’t just listen to their concerns—but turns concerns into action. I’m grateful that every single day, I get to wake up and do just that. With your continued support, we will continue not just fighting back against Trump’s lawlessness, but lowering the cost of living, expanding access to affordable healthcare, and combating the climate crisis.
With your support, I made history as the only first-term Democrat in the House to pass a law in this Congress—and it was on behalf of our veterans. With you, I hosted more than 30 town halls, worked to release nine of our neighbors from ICE and CBP’s illegal detention, and put more than a million dollars back into the pockets of Oregonians.
I launched an investigation into one of Trump’s Department of the Interior officials. I brought articles of impeachment against Kristi Noem. And I helped found the Democratic Doctors Caucus to fight against RFK Jr.’s medical misinformation.
All of this was possible because of you.
These are difficult times. But Oregonians have proved over and over again that even when the Trump administration does everything they can to create chaos and mistrust, they cannot divide us. We choose peace. We choose hope. And we choose our neighbors.
This work isn’t over. That’s why I’m running for re-election—and why I’m asking you to stick by my side.
We’re less than six months out from the primary in May. I’m fighting to bring back compassion, accountability, and science to the House and Senate. Are you with me? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_med_email-26q1?refcode=x_260127_electionfiling_act]

name: Tom Leonard
subject: Jan. 28th - Positive Path Newsletter
body:
[](https://sendy.right-strategies.us/l/cve9YluPeAoOO3uAO6KV4g/1l892l5ii3IokT0otdxbWbgQ/CgVQMBUqHH38t5IOVjrdEA)
---
Dear Friend,

While this past week was a cold one, it was very productive for our campaign. Here are some highlights:

• I attended a solar farm meeting in St. Johns and shared my thoughts, letting the local community know that I will always stand with them.
• I was a guest on Justin Barclay's Podcast, 'West Michigan Live'
• On Friday, I spoke to hundreds of leaders at the Northern Michigan Policy Conference.
• On Saturday, Nikki Snyder and I hosted another Virtual Education Town Hall
---
Things are heating up for our team, even in the bitter Michigan cold. Creating real solutions with a positive message and showing up in
local communities to meet the people we're fighting for are key to us.

This is what winning looks like.

**Building an Economy for Michigan Families**

I'm committed to building an economy that works for Michigan families, small businesses, and job creators, not special interests or big government.

Michigan's small businesses are the true backbone of our economy; they make up nearly all our state's companies and employ half our private workforce. That's why my plan starts by getting the government out of the way:

• A simple, pro-growth tax code that rewards hard work and expansion instead of punishing it.
• Restoring Right-to-Work so employers have the flexibility they need.
• Cutting red tape and streamlining licensing to help new businesses launch faster.
• Aligning education and training with real jobs in trades, tech, and manufacturing.

There will be no more corporate welfare. I'll eliminate the Michigan Economic Development Corporation and create the Michigan Business Action Center (MiBAC), a central hub that helps every business navigate regulations and grow, without picking winners and losers.

With these policies, and much more in our policy plan, 'The Path Forward' we will make Michigan a growth state again. Together.

**Protecting Local Communities against Big Tech and Data Centers**
---
Our campaign is committed to standing with Michiganders and their local communities against the abuses of Big Tech.

We are calling on the Legislature to end corporate welfare and pass a one-year moratorium on ALL data center construction in Michigan.

We've started a petition for this exact reason.

Sign on, share with your friends, and join us in this fight to protect Michigan's local communities.

Check it out and sign here: [www.protectmicommunities.com/](https://sendy.right-strategies.us/l/cve9YluPeAoOO3uAO6KV4g/YJIXOoAJWidBtSQo9o2QTw/CgVQMBUqHH38t5IOVjrdEA)

**Join the Team!**

It's with your help that results come.

We would love to have you join the team!

Volunteer Today: Sign up for phone banking, door-knocking, events, or hosting a meet-and-greet in your community. Your time makes all the difference! [Sign Up Here](https://sendy.right-strategies.us/l/cve9YluPeAoOO3uAO6KV4g/Lf5N763xvH7eiPI6dmvXZl2Q/CgVQMBUqHH38t5IOVjrdEA) And reach out to our Field Director, Tony, for more volunteer opportunities at tony@tomformichigan.com

Continue sharing our positive vision on social media - follow my X account's, [@Tom4Michigan](https://sendy.right-strategies.us/l/cve9YluPeAoOO3uAO6KV4g/z9ITmn8OFxDCLhkHSRDOAQ/CgVQMBUqHH38t5IOVjrdEA) and [@TomLeonard28](https://sendy.right-strategies.us/l/cve9YluPeAoOO3uAO6KV4g/J3ih398eRegqF763NuKUdUXg/CgVQMBUqHH38t5IOVjrdEA), my [Facebook page](https://sendy.right-strategies.us/l/cve9YluPeAoOO3uAO6KV4g/CEupZtSsDhsaujPQHF0892Qw/CgVQMBUqHH38t5IOVjrdEA), and my [Instagram](https://sendy.right-strategies.us/l/cve9YluPeAoOO3uAO6KV4g/763SEobT763763c19892YAZCEBxDiQ/CgVQMBUqHH38t5IOVjrdEA)
---
Thank you for continuing to support us in our fight week in and week out.

Together, we will make Michigan a growth state again, and build The Path Forward.

God bless you and your loved ones. Have a great week.

Best,
Tom Leonard
Candidate for Governor

To learn more, get involved, and donate visit [www.TomForMichigan.com](https://sendy.right-strategies.us/l/cve9YluPeAoOO3uAO6KV4g/aI05rqVVFm763f763e5He56nsw/CgVQMBUqHH38t5IOVjrdEA)

subject: He had a CIA badge in one hand and a martini in the other. Now he wants 10 million dollars.
body:
Two years ago, a CIA official sat across from our undercover journalist at a bar in Virginia. He ordered drinks. He flashed his badge. And then, unprompted,

| | [****](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zbmlvn37h3p722o147ahab0h1ntvrphj9o0rfmko_rp22sh2s8i6eor4slie1p72cjh2bs)
[****](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zq5hlk2nn7oac4e960akao8u577093h42mlt66f0_rp22sh2s8i6eor4slie1p72cjh2bs) Dear Friend,

Two years ago, a CIA official sat across from our undercover journalist at a bar in Virginia. He ordered drinks. He flashed his badge. And then, unprompted, he started talking.

He admitted the CIA withheld intelligence from the sitting President of the United States.

He described how FISA was weaponized to surveil Trump and his team.

He said all of this on camera.

We published it. America watched. And now he's suing me for **$10 million.**

**[](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z64lghmdno4t4iahadr7537a0qukj75b4v35d8p8_rp22sh2s8i6eor4slie1p72cjh2bs)**Help me defend the 1[**st Amendment by donating to my legal defense fund.**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zuojpruvsjcgll5t60966471im8qhje3pbu8ui58_rp22sh2s8i6eor4slie1p72cjh2bs)****

Let me be clear about what he's claiming: that our journalist committed "fraud" by using a dating app to meet him. That's it. A dating profile. Undercover investigative journalism is the same technique used by restaurant critics, investigative reporters, and 60 Minutes for half a century.

He also claims "wiretapping"—in Virginia, a one-party consent state where our recording was completely legal.

And the damages he's demanding? Compensation for "humiliation, depression, fear, and terror" caused by... the public hearing his own words.

This lawsuit isn't really about a dating profile or hurt feelings. **It's a message to every journalist in America: expose the intelligence community, and we will bury you in legal fees until you break.**

They've done it before. They'll do it again. [**Unless we prove it doesn't work**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zcqalrpfm4pkmr3c6g5m6teakphdcpeo1uvv44k0_rp22sh2s8i6eor4slie1p72cjh2bs).

I'm not settling. I'm not backing down. I'm taking this to discovery—where we'll subpoena documents, depose witnesses, and expose even more of what they've been hiding. If we have to, we'll take it to the Supreme Court.

[**But I can't do it alone**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zkbgfvji038663ut17bmlh3nvanv2m5scrg5llq0_rp22sh2s8i6eor4slie1p72cjh2bs).

Legal defense against a well-funded plaintiff—with what appears to be Deep State backing—costs hundreds of thousands of dollars. Every motion, every filing, every hour of attorney time adds up fast.

**[**Will you stand in the gap with me today?**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zlrf7uulko3tkjsabjn09amene2q9imhi1ssan88_rp22sh2s8i6eor4slie1p72cjh2bs)**

[**Your donation—whether $25 or $2,500—goes directly to legal defense**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zgj234oh2gf456i9bq9kqof8d2nmh3447t2e9fr0_rp22sh2s8i6eor4slie1p72cjh2bs), keeping our investigators in the field, and ensuring that the cost of telling the truth doesn't become too high to bear.

[**Your gift through Liberty Guard funds our defense so that we can keep fighting.**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zhspt9n217ic5usup37kecg7eolusu03a824uol8_rp22sh2s8i6eor4slie1p72cjh2bs)

He thought the camera would stay hidden. He thought his words would never see daylight. He thought wrong.

Let's finish what we started.

In Truth,
James O'Keefe
Founder and CEO
O'Keefe Media Group

**P.S.** Discovery is where the real fight begins—and where we often uncover more than the plaintiff bargained for. Your support today doesn't just defend this case. It funds the next investigation.

| | Friends,
At a recent [Attorney General debate](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0012bGY-1wFCvquyJBY6e_cki0iZFAKSSKm0dqWR3H2V-aQfWGnP41SahIBQaa7pSTuUT6HrqbTSAEGIEB6n-7Ce5B_-kvDorI7mXmjgaBgtIj2cMVXis-f_88bMsXDCWI8dRKdku0lBBnzbcBxQJGhqWLlTNSU0rXAJRsaG2CWHgAuFtBHDq1ltUA5bR_AZkGD&c=wOH-fvpI8j29LYzTddhRI9eehJFEs9DvKgk7O5GVK5EWhBYnjJVRkg==&ch=TesRet2R5cBCxPrcicVTy0_GKxuvZl0pRSfBKOkU01ZLKv4yKgC3gw==) hosted by the North Oakland Republican Club, we were asked an important question: Would you sue to stop sanctuary cities?

Here is my answer:
[Doug Lloyd on Sanctuary Cities](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0012bGY-1wFCvquyJBY6e_cki0iZFAKSSKm0dqWR3H2V-aQfWGnP41SahIBQaa7pSTu7ScpVLwSxdm74w0cO04_0ZVmgsKnDNrK5oM8rWix7jlG2fAMyw_Gaeb4x7hgjjWnIPhdEKtB8rxFcRmEz06Vz89PwBFnmJoQBFd1XELZCLxqK85Us8nKTy-Y9TURXornQEghpiqO_RNY1ivfMQ0-7A==&c=wOH-fvpI8j29LYzTddhRI9eehJFEs9DvKgk7O5GVK5EWhBYnjJVRkg==&ch=TesRet2R5cBCxPrcicVTy0_GKxuvZl0pRSfBKOkU01ZLKv4yKgC3gw==)
My opponent answered first and said that if elected Attorney General, he would use his power to sue any sanctuary city. That approach mirrors what we see from our current Attorney General and Democrat leadership who regularly disregard local control and use lawsuits as political weapons.
That answer may sound tough, but it ignores how the Constitution and the law actually work.
Here is the truth.
Cities are creatures of the state, and the state can only sue them if they violate a state law. There is nothing in the Michigan Constitution or in any statute that bans or prohibits sanctuary policies. Republican legislators, including Aric Nesbitt, have tried to pass legislation to change that, but those efforts were blocked by Democrat leadership.
Because no such law exists, sanctuary city policies are not illegal in Michigan. Filing lawsuits with no legal basis would get thrown out of court, waste taxpayer dollars, and embarrass the Attorney General's office.
Thankfully, there is a lawful and effective way forward.
Republicans are united in opposing sanctuary cities. The real solution is electing Republicans who can win and pass legislation that becomes law.
In the meantime, the Attorney General should work with Republican leadership in the House and Senate to cut state funding to sanctuary cities. President Trump has announced this approach at the federal level, and Michigan should follow suit. With a Republican Senate and governor, we can then pass legislation banning sanctuary city policies statewide.
Once funding is addressed, the Attorney General should coordinate with the federal government to form a joint task force. This would allow the Michigan State Police and the Attorney General's office to work directly with federal authorities to prosecute criminals shielded by these policies.
The Attorney General must also respect local control. We have seen the damage done when Democrats strip local control and force unwanted policies on our communities. Republicans cannot become activist hypocrites who play the same political games.
Michigan needs a serious leader who tells the truth, not someone who says whatever sounds good in a debate.
As Attorney General, I will protect all citizens, uphold the law, and deliver real results. I will not mislead voters or play political games.
Sincerely,
Doug Lloyd Eaton County Prosecuting Attorney Candidate for Michigan Attorney General

clean_body: The Lawful Path Forward | | | | | == | | | == | | Friends, At a recent == hosted by the North Oakland Republican Club, we were asked an important question: Would you sue to stop sanctuary cities? Here is my answer: == My opponent answered first and said that if elected Attorney General, he would use his power to sue any sanctuary city. That approach mirrors what we see from our current Attorney General and Democrat leadership who regularly disregard local control and use lawsuits as political weapons. That answer may sound tough, but it ignores how the Constitution and the law actually work. Here is the truth. Cities are creatures of the state, and the state can only sue them if they violate a state law. There is nothing in the Michigan Constitution or in any statute that bans or prohibits sanctuary policies. Republican legislators, including Aric Nesbitt, have tried to pass legislation to change that, but those efforts were blocked by Democrat leadership. Because no such law exists, sanctuary city policies are not illegal in Michigan. Filing lawsuits with no legal basis would get thrown out of court, waste taxpayer dollars, and embarrass the Attorney General's office. Thankfully, there is a lawful and effective way forward. Republicans are united in opposing sanctuary cities. The real solution is electing Republicans who can win and pass legislation that becomes law. In the meantime, the Attorney General should work with Republican leadership in the House and Senate to cut state funding to sanctuary cities. President Trump has announced this approach at the federal level, and Michigan should follow suit. With a Republican Senate and governor, we can then pass legislation banning sanctuary city policies statewide. Once funding is addressed, the Attorney General should coordinate with the federal government to form a joint task force. This would allow the Michigan State Police and the Attorney General's office to work directly with federal authorities to prosecute criminals shielded by these policies. The Attorney General must also respect local control. We have seen the damage done when Democrats strip local control and force unwanted policies on our communities. Republicans cannot become activist hypocrites who play the same political games. Michigan needs a serious leader who tells the truth, not someone who says whatever sounds good in a debate. As Attorney General, I will protect all citizens, uphold the law, and deliver real results. I will not mislead voters or play political games. subject: Legislative Update from the Gold Dome
body:
Read up-to-date information from your State Capitol
| | | | |
---
| The 2026 Legislative Session officially kicked off on Monday, January 12. I am honored to continue representing our community under the Gold Dome. >From now through early April, the Georgia General Assembly will meet to consider important legislation, including the annual state budget. These first few weeks are off to a great start.
As I begin my final Session before I hope to represent you in Congress, I want to thank you for the opportunity to serve a community I love -- we have more work to do! Please read below for an update on the latest from the Gold Dome.
---
| |
---
| LEGISLATIVE UPDATES
---
| |
---
| This year marks the second legislative Session of the 158th Georgia General Assembly. Each Session is Constitutionally set at 40 legislative days (committee days and days off do not count toward the 40). With the start of the 2026 Session now behind us, we've completed the opening stretch and are fully underway at the State Capitol.
We returned to work in a newly restored House Chamber. The renovation preserved the history and character of the People's House while bringing much needed updates -- a project that was completed remarkably quickly. The work began the day after last year's Session ended and wrapped up in December just before we returned. Whenever you are in Atlanta, please stop by to see the renovations.
The first order of business was adopting the legislative calendar for the year, officially setting Sine Die, the final day of Session, for April 2. The first week also included Governor Brian Kemp's final State of the State Address. This annual address gives the Governor an opportunity to outline his priorities for the Session and set the framework for budget discussions. Gov. Kemp focused heavily on lowering the cost of living for Georgians while continuing to invest in education, workforce development, public safety, and economic growth. He highlighted the remarkable $9.7 billion returned directly to taxpayers since 2021 and announced plans for another one-time tax rebate, along with a further reduction in the state income tax rate.
As we begin moving legislation this year, my own priorities for the Session are aligned with what I hear from folks at home. That starts with continuing to cut the state income tax and passing meaningful property tax relief, so families can keep more of what they earn and afford to stay in their own homes. I also remain focused on trying to ensure our local governments are addressing homelessness issues in a way that is compassionate but effective. You will see more on this from me very soon. I also remain focused on improving education outcomes with a strong emphasis on parental choice and literacy, and ensuring that we pass a balanced budget that spends taxpayer dollars conservatively and responsibly.
---
|
---
| Speaking of the budget, week two marked "budget week." While we did not meet on the House floor, the House and Senate Appropriations Committees held joint hearings throughout the week to review the Governor's proposed budgets. Each year, the General Assembly is Constitutionally required to pass a balanced budget, and these hearings are one of the first steps in that process.
We consider two budgets each Session: an amended budget for the current fiscal year and a budget for the next fiscal year. Georgia's fiscal year runs from July 1 to June 30, and the amended budget allows us to adjust spending based on updated revenue estimates. This year's proposals include major investments in education at every level, full funding of the HOPE Scholarship, and the creation of a new needs-based scholarship program called the DREAM Scholarship to help more students afford college. The budgets prioritize transportation improvements, public safety, rural economic development, behavioral health, and efforts to address homelessness. Critically for our area, it includes $200 million in additional funding for interchange conversions on Highway 316.
As we move forward, House budget subcommittees will begin working through the details before sending the budget to the full Appropriations Committee and, ultimately, the House floor. Early in the Session, most work happens in committees; later, the focus shifts to floor votes as bills move toward Crossover Day (March 6).
I appreciate the opportunity to represent you and will continue to keep you updated as the Session progresses and legislation begins moving through the House. As always, please don't hesitate to reach out with any thoughts on pending legislation.
---
| |
---
| BUDGET PRIORITIES
---
| In the Governor's budget recommendations, there are several projects that affect our community. These include:
* $200 million for construction of interchange conversions on Highway 316
* $11.43 million for the new University of Georgia School of Medicine
* $5.6 million for start-up costs for the new UGA School of Nursing
* $37.5 million for construction and equipment of the University of Georgia Science and Ag Hill Modernization project

The budget also includes:
* $1 billion tax rebate for all taxpayers
* $2 billion in extra roadway infrastructure investment
* $5.2 million to establish the State Law Enforcement Officers defined contribution retirement plan
* $611 million to fund $2,000 supplements for all state employees and teachers
* $325 million to fund needs-based Dream Scholarship program
* $50 million for homelessness grant programs
* $13.4 million for contraband detection systems in prisons

These are just a few highlights of the budget in its current form. I will keep you updated on these items and much more as the budget moves through the appropriations process. To view the entire budget proposal from the Governor, click [here](https://a89bm49ab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001QA4O782b3jlamCwH4ncM_hBlGifFfrsAV0SqJ_Ohh1HigA9xwe2iBBr-4eJlydH7bP0Glj0mF6ddgRREn81-TtcQQGms_rQXhE32KWpUr3jIECPGSzTisGoyg8R-XDWPMswfRZ4q7nukh4omzTm8Wzx7lP4lj5bUB4iqDPeV4t3EQuZznVt7bYqTPdlYyD1L&c=SJLIwGPfEnTAcZ_doFdCrkBDR2Z5Ht_eVQ2d-Ofr5JpjczdlI2_Cgg==&ch=uUMWM3c8Tui4slEVixihCE1KYQPn99Ao6jmyxxYO8oerdWy7c6BTsA==).
---
| |
---
| EVENTS AND CAPITOL VISITORS
---
| Each day, we begin Session with a Pastor of the Day. Each Pastor comes from a church throughout our state to deliver an inspirational message to all legislators. During the first week, my friend Rep. Clint Crowe from Butts County hosted Pastor Benny Tate. I've had the chance to meet Pastor Benny a number of times and always enjoy his message. He's one of the most effective communicators I've ever heard.
---
| |
---
| Over the last several days, our community experienced a significant ice storm. We were very blessed because it could've been much, much worse. I want to thank our linemen and all first responders who prepared and stood ready to assist those in need during the storm. I had the opportunity to visit the Georgia Power facility in Athens on Saturday to thank many of the folks working to keep the power on.
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| Last weekend before the storm hit, I attended the multi-county GOP meeting in Oglethorpe County. It was great to see friends and supporters from Madison, Taliaferro, Clarke, Oconee, Elbert, and Greene counties. I want to thank all of our volunteers for helping make the event a success.
If there is ever an event in our community where you'd like for me to attend or speak, please reach out and let us know. I also invite you to join us at the Capitol one day this Session to see your legislature at work.
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| 2026 COMMITTEE ASSIGNMENTS
---
| I look forward to representing our community on the following committees this year:
* Appropriations
* Insurance
* Transportation
* Ways & Means

These committees represent some of the most influential in the House, including the committee that handles the state's budget, tackles all tax related measures, and sets the direction for our state's transportation infrastructure.
---
| |
---
| WHAT'S NEXT?
---
| Over the next two weeks, we will complete through legislative day 14 of 40. While that means that we'll be over a quarter of the way through Session, the vast majority of major issues are still several weeks away from hitting the House or Senate floor. The final day of the 2026 Session will be April 2.
As always, we stand ready to help with any questions, comments, or concerns that you may have. Please reach out if I can ever be of assistance. Thank you for allowing me the honor to serve as your State Representative!
---

[Rep Marjorie Taylor Greene](https://open.substack.com/users/279031448-rep-marjorie-taylor-greene?utm_source=mentions) put out a tweet the other day responding directly to what is happening right now in Minnesota.
[| | | | | Former Congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene🇺🇸
---
@FmrRepMTG
I impeached Biden's Secretary of Homeland Security, Alejandro Mayorkas, those were my articles of impeachment that passed in the House of Representatives. I unapologetically believe in border security and deporting criminal illegal aliens and I support law enforcement. However,
| 2:56 PM * Jan 25, 2026 * 3.25M Views2.98K Replies * 2.87K Reposts * 28K Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/dd321609-d076-4ea4-a1c0-607c7ff09704?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
There are protests. There is federal enforcement activity. There is outrage. There is a familiar cycle of footage, reactions, commentary, and people choosing sides almost immediately. Videos are being zoomed in on, rewound, slowed down, framed, and now increasingly reconstructed by AI in ways that serve political slants rather than truth.
Greene's tweet tried to cut through that by offering a simple what-if.
Take what is happening in Minnesota. The protests. The federal presence. The enforcement actions. Now swap the labels.
Replace protesters against ICE under the Trump administration with January 6 protesters. Replace ICE agents with FBI agents operating under the Biden administration.
Keep everything else the same.
Same tactics. Same posture. Same justifications. Just different actors wearing different names.
Then ask yourself how you would feel about it.
It is not a complicated thought experiment. It is actually pretty basic. Most people should be able to arrive at that comparison on their own without being walked there. But the fact that it had to be spelled out says a lot.
What made this moment interesting was not the argument itself. It was who made it.
As [Saagar Enjeti](https://open.substack.com/users/1998730-saagar-enjeti?utm_source=mentions) framed it on Breaking Points, it took someone like Marjorie Taylor Greene, better known now as "Marjorie Traitor Greene," someone clearly associated with the Republican Party and the right, to say this out loud in order for people on that side to feel comfortable expressing outrage. To feel that maybe this was an overreach. That maybe a line was being crossed.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/85b47495-6ffb-41cc-b457-e762007a5a22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
That should set off alarms.
We are in a place where people do not evaluate state power, federal enforcement, or civil liberties based on principle first. They evaluate based on tribal permission. Who is allowed to say this. Who is allowed to feel this way. Whether speaking up will get you thrown out of your political group, your friend group, or publicly shamed online.
And when Saagar says that Greene's statement gives people on the right permission to feel that something is wrong, my reaction is not relief. It is sadness.
Why do you need permission at all?
### The Permission Problem...

## Landmark Social Media Trial Begins
A landmark jury trial against Meta, YouTube, and TikTok began Tuesday in Los Angeles Superior Court, marking the [first of several high-profile cases](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2O6yAUhJ8Gd1iAjX8Kitu4y223tDAcx2cDJoKTWH77lbOPsN1II32ab75u881iwP3-30YwtKZ5h6MEIII8l-TQhggebdopow2vYlM446yE6riQXA2ztxjOua28WQEUNBUY2XejHgc96GozWq_Q9E2vx0Uq1TaDdbLxwzguQmg1rBWaiyakGqQUYyvrZXSgrexECx5827FWgEdKuf5OuNMGazjTG3LtUqyC2YiehTX_mJqYmo7jqN2-uKtkarrQTE1CXrlnalpCco_lVQgy__XjH0H-8eMPdI_C07ryA2njMWXglLhLEThtWPgJNtcbxVBl458HhoCl61kr7tFi-EyiP_34NuonAAD__0O_hyM) in 2026 that could have major implications for regulation of social media companies. The case centers on a 19-year-old woman who alleges she became addicted to social media in her youth because of certain features like autoplay and infinite scrolling, leading to depression and suicidal thoughts. TikTok settled with the plaintiff Tuesday for an undisclosed sum, while [Snapchat settled](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGOszAQBeDTmM7IdgyBwsXf0OVvt0SDPQ6zsXEEkyBuvyJ7hO1GGunpfe_rNt6AEi33_5DRcSzjgvuWkBnXcSueIGUMBGXhlSC9NijpyKNRppVKS9ONASgdo62Ci4gGLxU6fW37pu-arqlmZ2PTg_YKfQww6ahB6RgMXC8wGd-0FbkzTWnTaa16q-up99iAbpXFgMG2wioMxGWtvwstPGNMR3njWvuSq-Rm5ucmLv-EGYQZ9n2v_bSdivMvzHCewgwZGSTTg8tDHuXFrwnlxyR_mfLjlBACeaayyIwLQ5IzQuJZmKFaXXjulBJt7VVYdc9A6dOB_zTc25mfAAAA___mIYXR) last week, leaving Meta and YouTube to face the jury. The trial has drawn comparisons to lawsuits brought against cigarette companies in the 1990s, with Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg expected to testify during the [six-to-eight-week trial.](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLtu4zAURL-G6iiQNPUqWLhRsYC33EUq4Vq8MpnwYZDXFvz3gZxPSDsDHMyZ_5flAj74dPsLEQ1teUm414BEWJaaVw8hovWQExUP4VEhh1dclFA9F5KrcbHgw2vRjTUbosJTg0YO_dRNYzd2jTMatusAkxKj1oNau-u6ybGzdjwJgcPQN94cNCHVKKWYtGyv04odyF5otGh1z7RA6ymX9jP7RA638MpPLO2aYxOMI7pXdjozNTM17_vexpqOjqkZE39UpmaHEMgxNWdyWJiaAyQboXzxtxYnrFT5GsDHyskB8R93_pbnDsqRI6YDBoWfz_Kf-PjzbIqx992H4Gs_MC1uEXx476Jfnfk06jsAAP__kqyKag)

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. # [What polarization actually looks like](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=185439545&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg1NDM5NTQ1LCJpYXQiOjE3Njk2MDk1OTIsImV4cCI6MTc3MjIwMTU5MiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.VA3hcOUApwJ2G6Gi1lrFx9oq_z8dEWbzorAYJ-tslWk)
### I've been comparing Fox News, New York Times, and Wall Street Journal headlines every morning. It's jarring.
| | [Ben Samuels](https://substack.com/@bensamuels)
---
| Jan 28
---
| [](https://substack.com/@bensamuels)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=185439545&utm_source=substack&isFreemail=true&submitLike=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg1NDM5NTQ1LCJyZWFjdGlvbiI6IuKdpCIsImlhdCI6MTc2OTYwOTU5MiwiZXhwIjoxNzcyMjAxNTkyLCJpc3MiOiJwdWItMjQ0MDM5OCIsInN1YiI6InJlYWN0aW9uIn0.szcGb5pZyCXcw8GP5xf7fNRnWM-1xmVSUYBSMSy0XHo&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=email-reaction&r=1hvr60)

| | [](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=185439545&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&isFreemail=true&comments=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg1NDM5NTQ1LCJpYXQiOjE3Njk2MDk1OTIsImV4cCI6MTc3MjIwMTU5MiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.VA3hcOUApwJ2G6Gi1lrFx9oq_z8dEWbzorAYJ-tslWk&r=1hvr60&utm_campaign=email-half-magic-comments&action=post-comment&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=185439545&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg1NDM5NTQ1LCJpYXQiOjE3Njk2MDk1OTIsImV4cCI6MTc3MjIwMTU5MiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.VA3hcOUApwJ2G6Gi1lrFx9oq_z8dEWbzorAYJ-tslWk)
---
| | [](https://substack..M9xGPb4uBCeSY1frlCsOykCBTWWFHctjvqZvzpC1Gg8?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/bensamuels/p/americas-split-screen-reality?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

_While researching this article, I started collecting screenshots of every morning 's top stories from Fox News, The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, and The Washington Post. _
_I 've been putting that online with **[What They're Reporting](https://substack.com/redirect/f1296ed3-3ac8-4463-9c9f-df8f584b6b50?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**, an Instagram page that compares how they're covering the news. It's fascinating to look at this stuff side-by-side--follow the account if you're interested._
[Follow What They're Reporting](https://substack.com/redirect/f1296ed3-3ac8-4463-9c9f-df8f584b6b50?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
The last two weeks of news have been defined by two stories: Trump's proposed acquisition of Greenland and the protests against ICE in Minneapolis, specifically how ICE agents have now killed two civilians.1
I often get asked some version of this question: "Republicans can see what's going on with Greenland/ICE/whatever insane and chaotic thing is happening right now. Why aren't they turning on Trump?"
The answer: **Republicans aren 't seeing what's going on**.
Intellectually, everyone understands that there's a divide between how Republican outlets versus mainstream ones cover the news. But when you look side-by-side, you get a sense for just how wide that divide really is.
[Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9iZW5zYW11ZWxzLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9hY2NvdW50IiwicCI6MTg1NDM5NTQ1LCJzIjoyNDQwMzk4LCJmIjp0cnVlLCJ1Ijo5MDUwMTE5MiwiaWF0IjoxNzY5NjA5NTkyLCJleHAiOjIwODUxODU1OTIsImlzcyI6InB1Yi0wIiwic3ViIjoibGluay1yZWRpcmVjdCJ9.pPyRrnfi653b3yK-AFx16UdLpOQYL6ZvsDzQ1S9_2pY?)
> _**Article summary:**_
> * _The headlines you see every morning vary wildly depending on where you 're getting your news. The screenshots below are vivid examples of that._
> * _Fox News hardly covered Trump 's threats against Greenland; their coverage of the protests and killings in Minnesota has, to date, blamed chaos on the "far left."_
> * _It 's hard to spin local news--you'll know if the potholes aren't getting fixed. But it's much easier to spin national news, because it's not something we immediately see._
>

### Republicans and Democrats have different top stories
Everyone knows this: Democrats and Republicans [consume and trust different media sources](https://substack.com/redirect/cce86cc9-051d-4f1a-816d-8398f9857329?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Over the last two weeks, I've been capturing what that concretely means. Here are screenshots of the top stories from _The New York Times_ , _The Wall Street Journal_ , and Fox News2 taken around 8:30 a.m. on Monday, January 19.3
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2fbab705-a899-4800-8c2c-96e06614d992?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
If you're reading the _NYT_ or the _WSJ_ , the top story was about a president threatening to invade an ally over a petty personal slight.
Fox News wasn't covering it at all. Their top story was about a "leftist mob," and I don't recall any Greenland news even being on their homepage that morning.
Now let's take a look at how these three media outlets have been covering the ICE protests in Minneapolis and the killings of Alex Pretti and Renee Good. Below is their coverage around 9:30 a.m. on Sunday, January 25.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a6253495-4843-4174-a587-5b23b360739b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And here were the top stories on the _NYT_ , the _WSJ_ , and Fox News taken around 6:50 a.m. on Monday, January 26.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9c12244b-1985-4a52-abf8-0b245116bf80?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Unlike the story with Greenland, where Fox News coverage was largely absent, they _are_ covering what's happening in Minneapolis. But they're taking a completely different angle. Where the _NYT_ and the _WSJ_ are covering the killing of a U.S. citizen, Fox News is focused entirely on "anti-ICE agitators" and "the far-left network that helped put Alex Pretti in harm's way."4
I'm not a newspaper editor. But from where I sit, Fox News is willfully missing the big picture. A U.S. President threatening to invade an ally is a much bigger story than protests at a church; the primary story in Minneapolis is the killing of a U.S. citizen, not what a former Vikings captain has to say on the topic.
This problem is even more acute on social media, by the way. But there's no good way to capture that in three screenshots--the problem there is much more immense and much more diffuse.
[Follow What They're Reporting](https://substack.com/redirect/f1296ed3-3ac8-4463-9c9f-df8f584b6b50?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
### Americans trust the news that they're consuming--and don't trust news coming from the other side
It's worth taking a closer look at precisely what this means.
Democrats are inclined to trust traditional news sources like newspapers and broadcast news. Republicans have very little trust in any of those institutions,5 and instead trust outlets like Fox News and Newsmax.6
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d9089ebb-f075-4f8c-a1a5-5f6a17a11837?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Source: [YouGov](https://substack.com/redirect/d9089ebb-f075-4f8c-a1a5-5f6a17a11837?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). This has been cropped in the middle (cutting out news sources like _Financial Times_ and _The Hill_) for simplicity and space constraints.
We can quibble about the biases in the _NYT_ or CNN newsrooms, which definitely exist, but they all aspire to, and work towards, nonpartisanship. Compare that to Fox News, which [explicitly calls itself](https://substack.com/redirect/b75ccba7-d173-4a2b-bcdc-1df6d0e0d39d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an "alternative to the left-of-center offerings of the news marketplace." Or to [Breitbart](https://substack.com/redirect/e30b37ae-7caf-48fe-a1ac-f20ee84f00d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): "original reporting curated and written specifically for the new generation of independent and conservative thinkers."7
So if you're wondering why people seem so immovable in their political views, this is a huge part of the reason. You and I might be outraged by what's happening with Greenland or what's happening in Minneapolis, but if Fox News is your primary source of information, you may not be getting this information at all.
And even if you are exposed to the coverage from the _WSJ_ , you're not even inclined to believe or trust it.8
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=185439545&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg1NDM5NTQ1LCJpYXQiOjE3Njk2MDk1OTIsImV4cCI6MTc3MjIwMTU5MiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.VA3hcOUApwJ2G6Gi1lrFx9oq_z8dEWbzorAYJ-tslWk)
### It's easier to spin national news than local news
Like a lot of the country, St. Louis was covered in snow last weekend. And at least where I live in St. Louis County, they did a pretty good job plowing the snow such that I could drive without too much issue on Monday.
During last year's big snowstorm, that wasn't the case in the city of St. Louis. (A reminder: St. Louis City and St. Louis County are distinct from one another.) The city was so bad about dealing with that storm that then-incumbent [mayor Tishaura Jones had to apologize](https://substack.com/redirect/d64f7359-9a5d-40aa-8d2c-a0202f40fb15?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and it may very well have [cost her the election](https://substack.com/redirect/a856c98c-4cfe-4525-b2bf-267dca71de46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).9
In 1979, something similar happened in Chicago: mayor Michael Bilandic [famously did such a bad job](https://substack.com/redirect/068d770c-4ac4-4757-afcd-fc5871f588ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) managing a blizzard in 1979 that he lost [that year's mayoral Democratic primary](https://substack.com/redirect/9ab89213-4a8b-45be-bce2-117c7258e932?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Why am I bringing this up? **Because in local politics, it 's a lot harder to hide what's going wrong**. If the snow isn't getting plowed, if the trash isn't getting picked up, if there are potholes on the streets, if kids aren't getting to school on time, messaging can only do so much. People on the ground know what's happening.
But that's not the case with national politics. When it comes to what's happening with Greenland, at Davos, or in Minneapolis, if it weren't on TV, in the media, or on social media, most of us wouldn't know what's going on. It may impact us long-term, but it doesn't affect our day-to-day like a pothole does.
And so media coverage--or media spin, in the case of what we're seeing from Fox News--matters a great deal more. And it's hard to change people's minds if everything that they know is coming from media and social media, rather than what they're actually seeing and experiencing themselves.
### No, not all hope is lost
In spite of all of this: people _do_ get information outside of their bubble. People watch videos online with their own eyes. They talk to friends and colleagues, some of whom don't agree with them and force them to reckon with their own opinions.10
And it means that some people, if slowly, do change their minds. Just look at how much [polling has shifted towards Democrats](https://substack.com/redirect/807f90a9-ad06-4584-a1a8-fcd66c9a73a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ahead of the '26 midterm elections.
But this process is slow; all of us, myself included, aren't keen to admit that we've been wrong about something in the past. It takes a lot to get us to change our minds.
Hopefully, the stories of the past two weeks are enough to start breaking through.
[Follow What They're Reporting](https://substack.com/redirect/f1296ed3-3ac8-4463-9c9f-df8f584b6b50?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
_**Feel free to share this post with someone who will find this interesting.** If you're reading this email because someone sent it to you, [please consider subscribing](https://substack.com/redirect/b6aca738-495b-4ffd-9e48-525a9e1009f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)._
1
On both fronts, what's happening is abhorrent. I'm an [ardent believer in the post-war world order](https://substack.com/redirect/a05f3dc2-39dc-4ebe-9306-31cdaaad9af3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and blowing up 80 years of alliances for something so cosmically stupid--and for such a [cosmically stupid reason](https://substack.com/redirect/2b90a50e-844a-46f8-bfba-c26ffee2afc6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--is unthinkable to me. And what's happening in Minnesota is un-American at best and authoritarian at worst.
2
ChatGPT [has the full rundown](https://substack.com/redirect/0d94d0c6-32c7-4e09-b198-16a32bd543a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) here, but _The New York Times_ and _The Wall Street Journal_ are italicized because they're publications, but Fox News isn't because it's a TV channel. Probably an outdated rule at this point, but that is what the style guide would say.
3
All Central Standard Time, just to be precise in what I'm sharing.
4
The "far-left agitators," [according to Fox News](https://substack.com/redirect/56b46f31-4431-49a1-bbfe-f53601eebfd6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), were group chats to help coordinate protests. At best, calling them "far-left agitators" is a stretch.
5
The one I can't wrap my head around here is The Weather Channel. Yes, the vast majority of Republicans trust The Weather Channel, but still less than Democrats do. Is there so much distrust among media that there's a sense that even The Weather Channel is feeding us fake news?
6
Traditional media outlets are, on the whole, more trusted than Republican-leaning outlets, in part because they're more likely to have the trust of independents and in part because even Republicans don't always trust Republican outlets. But the story is the chasm between Republican and Democratic trust in these news sources.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d9089ebb-f075-4f8c-a1a5-5f6a17a11837?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Source: [YouGov](https://substack.com/redirect/d9089ebb-f075-4f8c-a1a5-5f6a17a11837?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). This has been cropped in the middle (cutting out news sources like _The Economist_ and _The New Yorker_) just for space constraints.
7
I'm not talking about MSNBC/MS NOW in this article, but I think their coverage has tons of its own issues too.
8
It's also worth noting: in terms of exposure, Fox News and the _NYT_ are on similar footing. Different sources say different things (the story of this whole article!): [Fox News says](https://substack.com/redirect/5f87bf84-e2c1-4646-a30d-133a9f4c0326?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it draws more views than _The New York Times_ , whereas Similarweb says that [nytimes.com is slightly higher](https://substack.com/redirect/92ee295a-03eb-4adc-92d1-6c2a3788f934?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) than [FoxNews.com](https://substack.com/redirect/30351d13-543c-4351-8ce8-efe87938de19?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). In any event, they're in the same league.
9
Then again: Tishaura Jones [lost so badly to Cara Spencer](https://substack.com/redirect/236d8b0f-9cff-441c-9993-759119467962?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that it couldn't have _just_ been about the snow.
10
Don't pretend that posting on social media is having any impact, by the way. Not only does it do nothing to change anyone's mind, it's actually counterproductive--[Republicans and Democrats both dig in when presented with talking points from the other side](https://substack.com/redirect/890f1d59-9141-42d9-9525-b01b93d04e18?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
