name: The Editors at Broad + Liberty
subject: Former employees say Game Commission has toxic, retaliatory work culture
body:
News + editorial | Broad + Liberty Weekly Reads | | | |
---
| | | Good morning, and welcome to _Broad + Liberty_ 's Wednesday Weekly Reads!

As always, to stay up to date on late-breaking stories and analysis, [subscribe to our daily email list](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=49a548c5c9&e=b7b3eddce2) and get the best of _Broad + Liberty_ delivered straight to your inbox.
---
|
---
|
# **[1\. Two former employees accuse Pennsylvania Game Commission of toxic, retaliatory work culture](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=a72dbead50&e=b7b3eddce2)**
_By Todd Shepherd_ Two former employees of the Pennsylvania Game Commission say the commission’s Harrisburg headquarters fostered a toxic work environment in which the human relations department felt emboldened to target employees with harassment while upper management looked the other way. The commission called the claims “disingenuous.” Both women say once health issues became part of their work lives — whether through disclosure, accommodation requests, or related discussions — they were met with escalating criticism and discipline. One quit, one was fired. **Why It Matters.** Adding a twist is the PGC’s unique position in the commonwealth. It is not a cabinet-level “department” such as the state health department or department of education. Instead, the PGC operates independently of the General Assembly’s day-to-day control. Its nine commission members are appointed by the governor and approved by the state senate. It does not rely exclusively on legislative appropriations because it is largely sustained by hunting and fishing licenses and other related fees. This does not make accountability obscure, but does give the commission extra distance from the kind of oversight other departments in the commonwealth might consider routine. Everyone who spoke to this outlet about their story, or what they witnessed, all said the same thing about the PGC: It is largely a commission staffed with good people of good conscience who are extremely talented and devoted to the commission’s mission. The caveat, they allege, is that there is a small core of people who have had free reign to isolate and attack certain employees they don’t like, and that the commission’s upper reaches of management sat idly by. [_Continue Reading_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=466a8abb0b&e=b7b3eddce2)
---
|
---
|
# [**2\. Who can afford to live here anymore?**](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=619181e502&e=b7b3eddce2)
_By Wally Nunn_ People talk endlessly about the cost of buying a home — interest rates, bidding wars, low inventory. But that’s not what really determines affordability. For most families, the question is much simpler: “Can we afford this house month after month?” That’s where affordability lives or dies. And when you run the numbers in Delaware County — especially in working-class towns like Upper Darby — the answer is increasingly: **No, we cannot.** **Why It Matters.** The math plays out across the state, in Norristown, Coatesville, Pottstown, Bristol Township, Reading, York, and parts of Pittsburgh. Any place where you combine modest home values with high real estate taxes, families face housing burdens of 32 to 40 percent of their household income. This is not just mismanagement by one township or school district, though there is plenty of that. This is a structural flaw in how Pennsylvania funds local government and — especially — how it funds public education. Property taxes were never designed to carry this load. They do not adjust when wages stagnate. They punish seniors. They hit working families hardest. And they make it nearly impossible for first-time buyers to get a foothold in communities that were once affordable. This is what a systemic failure looks like. [_Continue Reading_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=5b5f2d6e60&e=b7b3eddce2)
---
|
---
|
# **3\. Lightning Round**
* [_Guy Ciarrocchi: Josh Shapiro went to Harrisburg and all we got was this lousy autobiography_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=c7c6800c16&e=b7b3eddce2)
* [_Christine Flowers: Minnesota church invaders deserve the FACE Act_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=d1baaca31c&e=b7b3eddce2)
* [_Kyle Sammin: Now would be a great time for everyone to chill out_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=d32c4fe5d4&e=b7b3eddce2)
* [_Howard Lurie: Renee Good was no ‘domestic terrorist’_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=6c6410898b&e=b7b3eddce2)
* [_Thom Nickels: Don Lemon is living the narcissist’s dream_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=923c42e7f5&e=b7b3eddce2)
* [_Paul Davis: On guns and crime — My interview with John Lott_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=eeb57d2776&e=b7b3eddce2)
* [_Seth Higgins: An assault on a SEPTA Bus — and what it reveals about modern politics_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=b2a30e21c5&e=b7b3eddce2)

---
|
---
|
# **4\. What we're reading**
We at _Broad + Liberty_ are a Pennsylvania-focused publication but, like much of the country, we’ve kept one eye on Minnesota this past month. We asked last week whether this might not be [_a good time to chill out_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=1fa9245735&e=b7b3eddce2) and now, we are hopeful that calmer heads are indeed prevailing. [_Ashleigh Fields writes in_ _The Hill_ _this week_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=9c969fb1da&e=b7b3eddce2) that Minnesota Governor Tim Walz and Border Czar Tom Homan are in communication about how to step back from the edge of civil unrest in Minneapolis. It’s a welcome sign. Federal and state governments need to work together to enforce the laws while not provoking riots. Is it possible? We hope so.

Colorado is a prime target. In 2024 when most of the nation took a hard right turn to Trump and the Republican Party, Colorado held the line--CO shifted 4 points more to the left of the nation.
Colorado bucked the trend then and has been staunchly anti-Trump since 2016. And now we need it to fight back against MAGA once more.
But here's the problem: long ago, CO voters approved an independent redistricting commission never anticipating that a cheater like Donald Trump would gerrymander districts in the middle of the decade to keep his party in power.
We need to respond aggressively to MAGA's all-out assault on democracy and free and fair elections, and that means approving emergency redistricting in Colorado to counter Trump's gerrymandering in red states.
To do that, we will need to pass a ballot initiative that would let voters approve a plan to flip three or even four GOP-held seats in Colorado from red to blue.

A closet, a camera and a setup: Tina Peters assaulted in prison then thrown into solitary
| | | | [](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
| | Hi friends,
Listen to today's Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.joinrmv.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.joinrmv.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.joinrmv.). Here is a summary of today's top stories:
**🏛️ Under the Golden Dome...** Lawmakers are already facing tough tradeoffs as the session opens, advancing [Medicaid cuts for disabled Coloradans](https://link.email.joinrmv.) without board approval, [reviving gender identity language](https://link.email.joinrmv.) in child custody law, and warning [prison capacity could be exhausted by 2026](https://link.email.joinrmv.) after years of closures—forcing costly decisions amid a strained budget.
🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** Tensions escalated as Denver Mayor Mike Johnston [pledged to resist ICE operations](https://link.email.joinrmv.), reigniting debates over sanctuary policies and public safety. At the same time, scrutiny intensified after [Tina Peters was assaulted by a violent inmate](https://link.email.joinrmv.) at La Vista prison and then placed in isolation, raising concerns about inmate safety, unequal treatment, and accountability inside the corrections system.
🇺🇸**On the National Stage...** Nationally, concerns over transparency and governance grew after an online platform briefly removed—and then restored—a [controversial paper on infant mortality and vaccines](https://link.email.joinrmv.), fueling censorship fears. Congress [moved closer to a partial shutdown](https://link.email.joinrmv.) as Senate Democrats resisted an ICE-related DHS funding provision, again pulling immigration policy into budget negotiations.
**🗣️ Commentary Spotlight...** A commentary argues [public trust is eroding](https://link.email.joinrmv.) as years of censorship, selective outrage, and institutional coverups come into focus, warning that narrative control is failing as Americans increasingly reject manipulation and demand accountability.
This is your Mountain Minute for Wednesday, January 28, 2026.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[A closet, a camera and a setup: Tina Peters assaulted in prison then thrown into solitary](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY A.L. GOODWIN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
[](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
On the evening of January 18, just after 9:00 p.m., Tina Peters was assaulted inside the La Vista Correctional Facility in Pueblo, Colorado—not in a yard or a common area, but in a narrow janitor’s closet, out of view of surveillance cameras.
Peters had been filling a portable swamp cooler, a task other inmates routinely refuse to do, even as the prison overheats in the dead of winter due to a failing HVAC system. To access the water tank, she pulled the unit into the cramped closet, positioning her head and upper body between the door and the cooler—leaving her physically pinned in a space barely wider than the machine itself.
As Peters maneuvered the unit, another inmate approached in an agitated state. The woman, a 29-year-old serving a six-year sentence for violently stabbing her fiancé three times in the back with a steak knife and stabbing her brother in the hand when he attempted to intervene, began yelling repeatedly, “You disrespected me.”
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
|
---
**[Mayor Johnston Promises Resistance if ICE Comes to Denver](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** [DENVER7](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
* **City leadership signals resistance to federal law enforcement:** Denver Mayor Mike Johnston publicly vowed to push ICE “out” of the city if federal immigration operations occur, signaling an intent to resist lawful enforcement and escalate conflict between local and federal authorities.
* **Sanctuary posture framed as public safety strategy:** Johnston argued Denver does not need federal involvement, claiming reductions in crime and homelessness justify keeping ICE out—despite federal authority over immigration and concerns that noncooperation undermines enforcement of existing law.
* **Rule-of-law concerns raised by critics:** The mayor’s comments revive fears that sanctuary-style policies place ideology over accountability, potentially discouraging cooperation with federal agencies and blurring constitutional lines between municipal power and federal jurisdiction.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
|
---

The only way we can continue to spread truth is with your support!
[DONATE TO ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
|
---
**[Democrats Revive Gender Identity Language in Colorado Child Custody Law](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** [COLORADO POLITICS](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
* **Democrats move to reinsert gender ideology into custody law:** Senate Bill 26-018 would revive language stripped from last year’s bill, requiring courts to consider whether parents “recognize” a child’s gender identity as a protected class factor in child custody cases.
* **Parental rights and free speech concerns resurface:** Critics warn the proposal could pressure parents to affirm gender ideology to avoid losing custody, echoing past objections that such provisions amount to compelled speech and state intrusion into family decisions.
* **Earlier backlash signals deep public unease:** Similar custody provisions were removed from HB 1312 after massive public testimony and bipartisan concern, with even Gov. Jared Polis expressing discomfort—yet Democrats are pressing ahead again despite ongoing lawsuits alleging First Amendment violations.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
|

**ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️ **
[****](https://link.email.joinrmv.)[**The Age of Gaslighting Is Ending**](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
[****](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**BY C. J. GARBO | COMMENTARY | JANUARY 27** _You don’t get to do this again. You don’t get another George Floyd. You don’t get another COVID. You don’t get another “mostly peaceful” summer of chaos You don’t get another shutdown. You don’t get another censorship campaign. You don’t get another government-media narrative that collapses the moment questions start getting answered._ __
[**When “affordable housing” means government-funded housing in Colorado**](https://link.email.joinrmv.) **BY CORY GAINES | COMMENTARY | JANUARY 26** _During one of my public notice crawls for Logan County/Sterling, there was a notice about a developer applying for a grant from the state to turn an empty parcel of land into an affordable housing development._
__
__[**There Is No Constitutional Right to “Protest”**](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
[****](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**BY MICHAEL J BADAGLIACCO "MJB" | COMMENTARY | JANUARY 26** _In the heated discourse surrounding civil unrest and public demonstrations, a common phrase echoes through media and activism: the right to “peacefully protest.” Contrary to popular opinion, this term appears nowhere in the United States Constitution. The document does not grant a specific right to protest at all. Instead, the First Amendment protects “the right of the people peaceably to assemble, and to petition the Government for a redress of grievances.”_ __[****](https://link.email.joinrmv.)__

We cannot allow ICE to get away with murders of American citizens in broad daylight. If ICE agents aren’t brought to justice, they will kill again.
| | | | | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=00156H_kBkH35tCaPAGjDUwWONsRsxUufSL0rxzpKwGF30ufRHO5Nwc-_DWzT6GaOTElgoGLZgto9BK0If_TvhpPCOxXh7R3Hl-7nSPouC4jqakCUsPwqFFurd33S06HDLtFMmbZEsM571mDhQaOteaHxY_teTkt41K2Vp25kxDN4nNM-hhdMq1ntgyRYDliuxoaZ16d89ebdVKg_Pc5OTugzP3StzicHO8Brb1f5HqppY=&c=-0_VB1scIkv7-rzkZE2I-Mkn5rs03mAcUhVaYXRVt4Eu-kSzNBZs4g==&ch=9qA0NbuQWioanX7F8fSBc6sBiju28DeG5NKFWypPiTlmvRzUBIFhlg==)

| Peter,
Are you angry yet? You should be.
The Trump administration's killers have claimed another life. Earlier this month, ICE agents shot and killed Renee Good -- a poet, a wife, and a mother of three. On Saturday, they killed Alex Pretti, an ICU nurse at the VA and a protester demanding accountability.
Two lives, two families shattered. And a rogue gang of masked killers that believe they can murder American citizens with impunity.
After Alex Pretti was killed, Trump promised a "very honorable and honest investigation." But here's the reality: the Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension and the FBI have been locked out. name: Ken Martin
subject: A note from the ground in Minnesota.
body:
---
Derek, Yesterday, I spent the day in my home state of Minnesota, and I wanted to share some photos and stories from our visit. For those of you who are on the ground in the Twin Cities, I hope that you are staying safe and warm. For those of you who are watching from afar, I hope this email can give you some insight into what things are like on the ground right now. First, we headed to the Minnesota DFL headquarters, where we had a conversation with my friends and former coworkers. [](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-dfl?refcode=em_20260128_5939_fr&amount=7&refcode2=5939_22930333_Xx8juF&akid=5939%2E22930333%2EXx8juF) _Meeting with my former team at the Minnesota DFL Party.[**If you are able, click here to donate to support the Minnesota DFL Party.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-dfl?amount=7&refcode=em_20260128_5939_fr&refcode2=5939_22930333_Xx8juF&akid=5939%2E22930333%2EXx8juF)_ The Minnesota DFL team has barely slept. In the wake of tragedy, this team had to help win two special elections. And, last night, DFL candidates Shelley Buck and Meg Luger-Nikolai clinched victories in their respective Minnesota House District 47A and House District 64A races. With these victories, Minnesotans now have two more Democratic champions who will fight to lower costs, protect health care, and protect our community from federal overreach and violence. From there, we headed to the Capitol to catch up with my friend, Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison. AG Ellison and I discussed how he is leading the charge to hold ICE accountable in the courts, and he shared what is giving him hope during these dark and difficult times. [](https://www.instagram.com/p/DUCQabXAb7D/?refcode=em_20260128_5939_fr) _Speaking with my friend, Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison.[**Click here to watch our full conversation.**](https://www.instagram.com/p/DUCQabXAb7D/?&refcode=em_20260128_5939_fr)_ After my conversation with AG Ellison, my team and I volunteered at a Minneapolis church that is providing supplies to families who are scared of leaving their homes, for fear of being targeted by ICE. We dropped off food and helped receive and organize donations. The church was bustling with activity. There was a steady stream of cars dropping off donations, and people showed up from all over the city to volunteer. Two of the most requested items were diapers and baby formula. [](https://platform.winnable.app/events/rapid-response-grassroots-call-with-dnc-llgmb?refcode=em_20260128_5939_fr&amount=7) _Delivering supplies to families in need._ Then, I was humbled to visit the memorial sites of both Renée Good and Alex Pretti. _At the memorial sites for Renée Nicole Good and Alex Pretti, January 27, 2026._ Renée Good and Alex Pretti’s lives were taken far too soon. Both were valued members of their community here in Minneapolis. Both were labelled immediately as “domestic terrorists” by the Trump administration. That couldn’t be further from the truth. Renée was a poet and a mother of three killed while monitoring ICE activity after dropping her kids off at school. Alex was an ICU nurse at the VA, who, before he was shot dead in the street, was helping a woman who was shoved to the ground by federal agents. Yesterday, my team and I paid our respects to these Minnesotans who embodied our values. We mourn their senseless deaths, and stand with all who have faced brutality at the hands of Trump’s federal agents. This month of so much heartbreak and fear for Minnesotans has only steeled our resolve. But I also know we are not alone. The country is watching and with us. Trump may have thousands of federal agents, but we have our neighbors. And if we have learned anything from the movement in Minnesota, it’s that there’s strength and power in community, and our resistance makes a difference. On Monday, the news broke that Greg Bovino, the public face of Customs and Border Patrol who oversaw crackdowns in Los Angeles, Chicago, and Minneapolis, would be demoted and removed from that role. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. * And when I take a tough vote in the State Senate, I show up for my constituents and explain why, face to face — instead of hiding.

clean_body: I'm not running from what I stand for. = = Our nation’s politics have been so discouraging for so long that one refrain I hear a lot is that politicians are all the same. So I want to make it very clear: my opponent Bill Huizenga and I are not the same. Here are some things that Huizenga has done that I would NEVER do: He voted to give himself a $50,000 special-interest tax cut. It was part of the same Big Ugly Bill that decimated funding for food stamps and gutted health care access for thousands of your neighbors. He voted AGAINST funding critical Affordable Care Act benefits — when even several of his fellow Republicans broke ranks and supported the funding. So if, like most people, you saw a big spike in your premiums this year, Huizenga’s vote is a major reason why. He REFUSED to take a stand against the violent and lawless actions of ICE agents under Trump. When MI-4 constituents attempted to visit Huizenga’s office and peacefully share their views about ICE’s abuses of power, his staff wouldn’t even open the door to hear them out. And here are some things that I’ve done that Huizenga would never do: In the Michigan state legislature, I worked hard to expand Medicaid and increase health care access across our state — instead of making health care harder to get. I worked across the aisle to cut taxes for seniors and working families — instead of prioritizing billionaires. When Donald Trump puts the wellbeing of our community in jeopardy — by cutting food stamps, hiking grocery prices, or taking away basic freedoms — I speak out instead of falling in line. And when I take a tough vote in the State Senate, I show up for my constituents and explain why, face to face — instead of hiding. So, there’s a world of difference between what I stand for and what my opponent stands for in this race — and that’s why winning here in MI-4, and flipping the House blue along with it, couldn’t be more important. = | | = Thank you, Sean | Email is one of the best ways we keep supporters updated about Sean McCann’s campaign. body:
What is flipping this seat worth to you?
|
# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/2365?source=&t=1&akid=432%2E124072%2EjU81Pz)
**[Peter, asking for your financial contribution isn’t my favorite part of campaigning, and I know you get a lot of these, but with a critical end-of-month deadline in just a few days, I need a few committed supporters to chip in. Your $5 donation could make the difference between victory and defeat in this toss-up race.](https://act.roycooper.com/go/5178?amount=5&t=7&akid=432%2E124072%2EjU81Pz)** **Service is a privilege, Peter.** It’s why I have wholeheartedly dedicated my life to giving back to this nation that I love. It’s why I am running in one of the closest Senate races on the map — the toughest fight of my career. Because here’s something else that I believe: _Taking back this seat and returning power to the people is worth any fight._ And it’s one that I can’t win alone. Your contribution today could help us stay ahead of my far-right opponent in the polls — which have tightened in recent days. It could allow us to keep up with the GOP’s powerful PACs and mega-donors, all of whom are ready to pour money into NC to try to defeat me. It could determine whether we elect a leader who’ll be accountable to the people, or one who would continue to rubber-stamp anything President Trump desires. **[Peter, I have a question for you: Is $5 worth it to YOU to help flip this seat blue for the first time since 2008? If you’re with me, I’m counting on your contribution before our January deadline.](https://act.roycooper.com/go/5178?amount=5&t=8&akid=432%2E124072%2EjU81Pz)** | [DONATE $5](https://act.roycooper.com/go/5178?amount=5&t=9&akid=432%2E124072%2EjU81Pz)

Roy Cooper

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

There are families grieving right now. Communities trying to make sense of fear that never should have been normalized in the first place. And still, people are showing up. Calling their members of Congress. Speaking at hearings. body:
It’d mean a lot to me if you read this.
#
I was sworn in as Delaware’s representative in Congress one year ago this month — the same month Donald Trump was inaugurated as president for the second time.
I recently published an op-ed in the Delaware News Journal, reflecting on my first year in Congress. In many ways, this year has felt like a decade.
In this op-ed, I wrote about the work I’ve done for my state, the fights I’ve taken on, what’s ahead as we approach midterms, and why I consider myself the luckiest member of the House.
I hope you’ll take just a few minutes to read it.
— Sarah
* * *
McBride: I fight to protect Delaware. And I'll keep going
_Sarah McBride_
_January 14, 2026_
When I was sworn in as Delaware's member of Congress, I made a simple promise: I would work with anyone willing to deliver for Delaware, and I would stand up to anyone who would hurt Delawareans.
These last twelve months have felt like a decade in many ways. Time and again, we have seen the president sowing chaos and endorsing cruelty — striking fear into the hearts of immigrant neighbors, disregarding due process, firing public servants and attacking the foundations of the American health care system. Meanwhile, families across Delaware are facing rising utility bills, housing costs, and grocery prices that don't match their paychecks.
This is the reality that has shaped my first year in Congress.
**I'm focused on protecting Delawareans**
From day one, I've focused on protecting Delawareans — because a government for and by the people must respect the rule of law, not the whims of the powerful and wealthy few. That meant standing up to political appointees who sought unauthorized access to Americans' personal data, pushing for transparency and accountability from the White House, and defending Congress's constitutional role in decisions about war.
We've seen the consequences when those guardrails fail — when wealthy donors are given a blank check to summarily fire civil servants and hollow out federal agencies Congress created to serve the public.
We also witnessed relentless attacks on the American health care system: the largest cut to Medicaid in our history, mass firings of health care workers, and partisan attacks in the research and institutions that keep us safe from disease. Science — not ideology — should guide decisions that affect people's health. That's why I supported legislation to protect vaccine access, fought to restore and strengthen Medicaid funding, reinstate federal health workers and extend Affordable Care Act tax credits — something we are much closer to now than when my Democratic colleagues and I started that effort.
I'll be the first to admit it: it can feel like Congress isn't doing enough to address everyday concerns. But after my first year in office, I'm proud to say I know that progress is still possible, despite a loud, divided and too-often dysfunctional Washington, when we listen to one another and put people over politics.
Every day in Washington, while I work to defend our democracy and address the cost of living, Delawareans reach out to my office for help navigating federal bureaucracy. A Social Security notice demanding tens of thousands of dollars because of an administrative error. A delayed tax refund. A stalled SBA loan. A grandmother unable to access her Medicare coverage. A veteran denied the benefits they earned in uniform.
To the people facing these challenges, they mean everything. In every constituent we serve, we learn how to make government deliver better for all of us.
That's why I'm most proud that my office helped over 800 Delawareans this year, returning nearly $4 million directly to families. Oftentimes, government isn't abstract — it's whether a problem gets solved or a door gets slammed shut.
Delivering for our neighbors also means bringing resources home. This year, working alongside Senators Coons and Blunt Rochester, we helped secure over $200 million in federal grant funding for Delaware communities, hospitals, schools, and local governments — along with more than $76.4 million of new direct investment across our state.
When I was elected, I hadn't hoped to serve in the minority. So, yes, I have real disagreements with my Republican colleagues. When I need to stand up to policies that would hurt Delaware, I do — and always will. But Delawareans know something Washington sometimes forgets: you can stand for your values and still work together where common ground exists. That's how we deliver results.
I introduced five new bills, all with bipartisan support, all shaped directly by conversations with Delawareans — from consumer protection to supporting farmers. One of my bills that would expand investment for entrepreneurs and small businesses passed the House unanimously this past summer.
I led a bipartisan effort to restore funding the Trump administration cut from Delaware's Manufacturing Extension Partnership, protecting small and mid-sized manufacturers and good-paying jobs, and helped secure bipartisan funding for Delaware-developed cooling technology that reduces data centers' energy and water use and eases pressure on utility costs.
And when the Trump administration moved to cut Medicare's funding for home health care, I worked across the aisle to stop it — preserving nearly $1 billion so seniors can receive care at home and caregivers can keep doing their jobs. I've continued my work to expand paid family and medical leave nationally and support fair wages, because no one should have to choose between their family or their wellbeing and their livelihood.
Supporting our veterans has remained a priority — from protecting earned benefits, to cutting red tape at the VA, to ensuring servicemembers are paid even during a government shutdown.
**I'm proud of Delaware**
I consider myself the luckiest member of the House. Not everyone gets to represent the greatest state in the Union. That's why I also spent this year traveling across Delaware — joining town halls and roundtables, touring small businesses, and taking over 360 meetings with neighbors across 35 towns and cities. Those moments at home remind me of the true Delaware way: democracy works best when we focus less on ideology and more on outcomes— less on noise and more on neighbors.
It is the privilege of my lifetime representing our state in the House of Representatives. As I begin my second year, I'm more clear eyed than ever about the work ahead. I'm grateful to the people of Delaware for trusting me with this responsibility.
* * *
**Thank you for reading!** Sarah is working every day to push back against Trump’s billionaire agenda, hold Republicans accountable for the harm they’re causing, and deliver real solutions to make life more affordable for working families. **None of that is possible without this grassroots team.** **[If you’re able, can you pitch in $5 to defend Sarah’s seat, retake the House, and deliver real results for working people?](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260128-1.S8LSZf&refcode=em20260128-2738&amount=5&t=1&akid=2738%2E21716%2EcOz8x1)** **[Donate $5 »](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260128-1.S8LSZf&amount=5&refcode=em20260128-2738&t=20&akid=2738%2E21716%2EcOz8x1)**

Peter –
A new year is supposed to bring new beginnings. But as January comes to an end, one thing hasn’t changed: the fight to protect our democracy and our Constitution is as urgent as ever.
Across the country, voting rights remain under attack, and Trump continues to threaten our democracy. We’ve seen efforts to undermine free and fair elections, weaken constitutional safeguards, and erode the rule of law. These threats didn’t disappear when the calendar turned, and neither did our responsibility to confront them.
That’s why this moment matters so much.
As Attorney General, Jena will be on the front lines of this fight: defending voting rights, enforcing the law without fear or favor, and upholding the Constitution no matter who is in power. This isn’t about politics. It’s about protecting the foundation of our democracy and ensuring that every eligible voter can make their voice heard.
The end of the month and the beginning of a new year are critical checkpoints for this campaign. What we build right now will determine whether we have the strength and resources to stand up for democracy when it matters most.
If you believe in protecting voting rights, defending the Constitution, and stopping Trump’s illegalities, we need you with us. Chip in $25 right now to help us end the first month of the new year strong! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/2601-q1-jg?refcode=260128-email&amount=25]
Thank you for standing up for our shared values – this month, this year, and for the long fight ahead.

First Lady Melania Trump **[rang the New York Stock Exchange opening bell](https://substack.com/redirect/e963b5ff-4285-46b2-b8d1-6b0894a4dbc9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/e963b5ff-4285-46b2-b8d1-6b0894a4dbc9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)Wednesday to promote her self-titled documentary, "Melania," which offers an intimate look at the 20 days leading to President Trump's 2025 inauguration and premieres Thursday at the Trump-Kennedy Center before a global theatrical release.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e963b5ff-4285-46b2-b8d1-6b0894a4dbc9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Symbolic Bell Ringing** : Melania, in a sleek black dress, pressed the button amid cheers from traders and received a custom engraved commemorative plate from NYSE President Lynn Martin--a first for the exchange.
* **Documentary Production Details** : Directed by Brett Ratner and co-produced by Melania, the Amazon MGM Studios film stems from a $40 million licensing deal, featuring exclusive behind-the-scenes footage of inauguration preparations and White House transition moments.
* **Premiere and Release Plans** : The red carpet premiere occurs Thursday night at the renamed Trump-Kennedy Center in Washington, with simultaneous screenings in 20 venues; it hits theaters worldwide on January 30, 2026.
* **Cultural Impact Emphasis** : Melania highlighted storytelling's power in her remarks, stating cultural influence rivals economic power and films foster emotional connections, positioning her project as part of a great American tradition.

# S&P 500 smashes through the 7000 barrier for the first time ever
The S&P 500 **[surged above 7,000 for the first time in history](https://substack.com/redirect/1f9da3a2-13c8-4fe2-9114-f699cdcb106d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on Wednesday, climbing 0.3% at the open amid unrelenting AI optimism fueled by ASML's record chip orders, as Wall Street gears up for the Federal Reserve's rate decision and pivotal earnings from Microsoft, Meta, and Tesla.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1f9da3a2-13c8-4fe2-9114-f699cdcb106d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **AI Demand Surges Strongly** : ASML reported record €13.2 billion in Q4 orders far above expectations, signaling sustained AI infrastructure growth and boosting chip stocks like Nvidia, Intel, and Micron.
* **Fed Decision Looms Large** : The Federal Reserve is widely expected to hold rates at 3.5%-3.75%, with focus shifting to Chair Powell's comments for hints on potential 2026 rate cuts.
* **Big Tech Earnings Await** : Microsoft, Meta Platforms, and Tesla report after the close, with investors scrutinizing AI spending, robotaxi progress, and cloud growth amid high expectations.
* **Chip Sector Leads Gains** : Intel jumped nearly 9%, Micron nearly 4%, and Nvidia added 2% on positive AI signals including China's approval of massive Nvidia GPU imports.

# Gold hits record $5300 per oz
Gold surged to an[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/cd50666b-9c08-41f0-9bd4-7fd0c3906cd5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[all-time high above $5,300](https://substack.com/redirect/cd50666b-9c08-41f0-9bd4-7fd0c3906cd5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** an ounce on Wednesday as President Trump's downplaying of a plunging US dollar fueled a massive safe-haven rush. The precious metal's 22% year-to-date gain reflects escalating geopolitical risks, dollar weakness to near four-year lows, and investor flight from bonds and currencies amid policy uncertainty.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/cd50666b-9c08-41f0-9bd4-7fd0c3906cd5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Dollar Plunge Accelerates Rally:** Trump's comments dismissing dollar concerns drove the currency to its weakest level in nearly four years, boosting gold by making it cheaper for global buyers and sparking rapid retail investment inflows.
* **Geopolitical Risks Mount:** Threats of tariffs on allies like South Korea and Canada, plus potential actions in Greenland and Venezuela, heightened global tensions and triggered a flight to precious metals as safe havens.
* **Fed Dovish Shift Bets Grow:** Traders anticipate a less independent Federal Reserve with possible aggressive rate cuts, favoring non-yielding assets like gold; analysts see further upside barring short-term corrections.
* **Silver Joins Explosive Gains:** The white metal surged nearly 60% year-to-date, approaching prior records near $117 an ounce, amid broader precious metals volatility and strong investment demand.

# Starbucks US Sales surge ends two-year drought
Starbucks reported its **[first positive US comparable store sales growth in two years](https://substack.com/redirect/8035f0b9-f76d-4bd1-8524-2c4c431e8640?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/8035f0b9-f76d-4bd1-8524-2c4c431e8640?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)during fiscal Q1 ended Dec. 28, with a 4% rise driven by higher traffic and ticket size, as CEO Brian Niccol's "Back to Starbucks" turnaround strategy gains momentum and beats expectations for the key market.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8035f0b9-f76d-4bd1-8524-2c4c431e8640?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **US Turnaround Accelerates** : North America same-store sales climbed 4%, exceeding forecasts of 2%, marking the first positive growth since fiscal Q1 2024 with 3% transaction increase and 1% average ticket boost.
* **Global Momentum Builds** : Worldwide comparable sales rose 4% for the second straight quarter, surpassing estimates of 2%, highlighting broad recovery progress.
* **China Delivers Strong Gains** : Same-store sales in China jumped 7% above expectations, fueled by 5% foot traffic growth and 2% higher ticket size amid recent stake sale to Boyu Capital.
* **Mixed Bottom Line** : Adjusted EPS of $0.56 missed analyst targets of $0.59 due to turnaround costs and coffee price pressures, though revenue hit $9.9 billion beating estimates and stock rose over 7%.

# Mamdani demands millionaire tax hike to cover $12 Billion black hole
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani called Wednesday **[for higher taxes on the wealthy and corporations](https://substack.com/redirect/ca26ac94-a812-435e-bac2-9c354cf6e14c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to close a staggering $12 billion-plus budget deficit he blamed on prior fiscal mismanagement, dismissing business fears of capital flight while vowing transparency and savings in the nearly $116 billion FY 2026 budget.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ca26ac94-a812-435e-bac2-9c354cf6e14c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Millionaire Surcharge Proposed:** A flat 2% tax targets individuals earning over $1 million annually to generate revenue for the city's shortfall.
* **Corporate Rate Increase Urged:** Raising the city's corporate tax to 11.5% aims to match New Jersey's level and boost funds amid the crisis.
* **Deficit Scale Highlighted:** The projected $12.6 billion gap over two years exceeds Great Recession levels due to alleged mismanagement by predecessors.
* **Savings Measures Touted:** Mamdani criticized wasteful spending like a $600,000 unusable AI chatbot as part of broader efficiency efforts to complement tax hikes.

# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124215674/597924767/336227065?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDE1MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmMmE3ZjAyNi03YWZjLWYwMTEtOGQ0Yy0wMDIyNDgyZDI3OWIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=tLG5rwjIpKKVdcelfq0zDh7rLtaBax1VvSB-Vb4-7n8=)
Peter,

At the end of this message, we’re going to ask you to **[chip in $3](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124215675/597924768/336227065?refcode=em-1.28.26-all-b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDE1MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmMmE3ZjAyNi03YWZjLWYwMTEtOGQ0Yy0wMDIyNDgyZDI3OWIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=tLG5rwjIpKKVdcelfq0zDh7rLtaBax1VvSB-Vb4-7n8=)** ahead of our first end-of-month fundraising deadline of the election year.

But before we do, there are a few things you need to know about the state of this race:

clean_body: Our new endorsements to take back power in Texas | = Hi Peter, I have some exciting news to share with you: Today, EMILYs List is endorsing two powerhouse Democratic pro-choice women running to flip Republican seats in Texas and turn the state blue. ******=**** | = These women are boldly stepping up to flip critical seats, protect our rights, and win some of the toughest state-wide races in the country: In the race for governor, Gina Hinojosa is running to create a brighter future for all Texans. Born and raised in the Rio Grande Valley, Gina has dedicated her life to public service as a union lawyer, a proud member of Austin’s school board, and a state representative. Every step of the way, Gina has fought to make Texas a state where families, small businesses, and working Texans can thrive. In the race for U.S. Senate, Jasmine Crockett is running as a fierce advocate for everyday Texans. As a public defender, community organizer, and co-chair for the Harris-Walz campaign, she’s never backed down from speaking truth to power. Jasmine will fight to give Texans the faithful representation in the Senate that they deserve, no matter who she’s up against. Winning these races won’t be easy. Republican groups will invest HEAVILY to keep Texas under their control — and if we’re going to help Gina and Jasmine build the campaigns they need, we need to move quickly. ****=****** If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue, your donation will go through immediately: = | = ---|--- = | = = | = Thanks for your help, Ben Ray (he/him/his) Deputy Chief Campaigns Officer, Federal and Gubernatorial, EMILYs List = | | | | ---|---|---|---|--- Thank you for being a supporter of EMILYs List. name: Scott Peters
subject: Accountability & transparency
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Scott Peters for Congress
body:
---
| | Peter,

ICE agents’ lack of transparency and accountability, and insufficient training, has proven to have deadly consequences. And I won’t stand by while it continues unchecked.

Instead of focusing on serious threats, ICE is chasing arrest quotas and sweeping up everyone in their path, including children and even U.S. citizens. And despite its immense funding (which Trump has doubled while in office), agents are still not held to the same training and accountability standards as our local police.

That’s why I introduced legislation to restrict excessive use of force by ICE. Introduced back in November, this bill would limit military-style tactics, require body cameras, improve training, and make sure agents intervene when colleagues act unlawfully.

[If you agree that ICE agents must be reined in and held accountable, please add your name here.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124215995/597925550/890776915?refcode2=677c4902-7bfc-f011-8d4c-0022482d279b&refcode=SP_EM_PT_180DO_260128_2_2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzkvMS84ODA2MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2NzdjNDkwMi03YmZjLWYwMTEtOGQ0Yy0wMDIyNDgyZDI3OWIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Fa3AX39DNWhgIwH4P548gcYseiE5EPOQ-XBFOI6IdDA=&emci=577c4902-7bfc-f011-8d4c-0022482d279b&emdi=677c4902-7bfc-f011-8d4c-0022482d279b&ceid=5258741) | | **[SIGN ON](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124215998/597925551/890776915?refcode2=677c4902-7bfc-f011-8d4c-0022482d279b&refcode=SP_EM_PT_180DO_260128_2_2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzkvMS84ODA2MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2NzdjNDkwMi03YmZjLWYwMTEtOGQ0Yy0wMDIyNDgyZDI3OWIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Fa3AX39DNWhgIwH4P548gcYseiE5EPOQ-XBFOI6IdDA=&emci=577c4902-7bfc-f011-8d4c-0022482d279b&emdi=677c4902-7bfc-f011-8d4c-0022482d279b&ceid=5258741)**

Last year, ICE agents stormed a small neighborhood restaurant in our district. They slammed the owner against a wall, handcuffed workers, and used flash-bang grenades on bystanders – all to arrest four peaceful dishwashers, not violent criminals.

That kind of conduct makes no one safer, Peter.

[It’s time to end this unchecked aggression against civilians and restore transparency in law enforcement. If you agree, add your name here.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124216000/597925552/890776915?refcode2=677c4902-7bfc-f011-8d4c-0022482d279b&refcode=SP_EM_PT_180DO_260128_2_2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzkvMS84ODA2MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2NzdjNDkwMi03YmZjLWYwMTEtOGQ0Yy0wMDIyNDgyZDI3OWIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Fa3AX39DNWhgIwH4P548gcYseiE5EPOQ-XBFOI6IdDA=&emci=577c4902-7bfc-f011-8d4c-0022482d279b&emdi=677c4902-7bfc-f011-8d4c-0022482d279b&ceid=5258741)

Peter,

Late last week, the House voted on a funding bill that will send resources to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including ICE. I voted **no** on that bill. The events from this weekend in Minnesota only make me more confident that I made the right decision.

By now, many of you have seen the videos of the recent ICE shooting in Minneapolis. It is heartbreaking, disturbing, and downright cruel. It is also a pattern we are seeing unfold in real time.

ICE promised to rid our country of the worst of the worst—but instead—American citizens are being targeted, families are being torn apart without cause, and legal immigrants are having their status revoked or ignored. Our communities are flooded with fear, and our own citizens are now questioning if practicing their First Amendment rights will also lead to their untimely death. Yet the Trump administration is standing firmly behind their efforts—going so far as to try and stop local law enforcement from being able to conduct a thorough investigation of this weekend's death. _How can that be?_

As Secretary of DHS, Kristi Noem is responsible for this pattern of brutality, and she should be fired immediately or resign in disgrace. As president, Donald Trump must own his involvement in the militarization of ICE. It is not enough to ask for accountability; we need direct action to stop this devastating path our country is headed down.

I voted **against** funding DHS without additional oversight. I voted **against** a bill that failed to include clear guardrails, failed to strengthen transparency, and failed to rebuild trust between law enforcement and the communities they serve. I voted to stand firmly **against** the atrocities that we are seeing today that have no place in the United States of America.

Public safety should never come at the expense of people's rights, dignity, or lives. Every vote I take is to ensure our government is working for the betterment of the American people.

Thank you for standing with me,

Kim Rep. Kim Schrier is a doctor, scientist, and mom, fighting for Washington's 8th District in Congress. clean_body: It is not enough to ask for accountability; we need direct action to stop this devastating path our country is headed down. Peter, Late last week, the House voted on a funding bill that will send resources to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including ICE. I voted no on that bill. The events from this weekend in Minnesota only make me more confident that I made the right decision. By now, many of you have seen the videos of the recent ICE shooting in Minneapolis. It is heartbreaking, disturbing, and downright cruel. It is also a pattern we are seeing unfold in real time. ICE promised to rid our country of the worst of the worst—but instead—American citizens are being targeted, families are being torn apart without cause, and legal immigrants are having their status revoked or ignored. Our communities are flooded with fear, and our own citizens are now questioning if practicing their First Amendment rights will also lead to their untimely death. Yet the Trump administration is standing firmly behind their efforts—going so far as to try and stop local law enforcement from being able to conduct a thorough investigation of this weekend's death. How can that be? As Secretary of DHS, Kristi Noem is responsible for this pattern of brutality, and she should be fired immediately or resign in disgrace. As president, Donald Trump must own his involvement in the militarization of ICE. It is not enough to ask for accountability; we need direct action to stop this devastating path our country is headed down. I voted against funding DHS without additional oversight. I voted against a bill that failed to include clear guardrails, failed to strengthen transparency, and failed to rebuild trust between law enforcement and the communities they serve. I voted to stand firmly against the atrocities that we are seeing today that have no place in the United States of America. Public safety should never come at the expense of people's rights, dignity, or lives. Every vote I take is to ensure our government is working for the betterment of the American people. Thank you for standing with me, Kim Rep. Kim Schrier is a doctor, scientist, and mom, fighting for Washington's 8th District in Congress. This is one of the most competitive districts in the country, so we need your help to keep Kim in Congress. Hi,
After serving our country for 35 years in the Navy, I was removed from my position by Pete Hegseth without reason.
I spent my entire life in service to this country, always putting the mission and the people above myself. But when I was forced out, I had a choice: go out quietly, or _find a way to keep serving._
I’ve always lived by three simple ideals: honor, integrity, and respect. **That’s why I’m running for Congress in South Carolina’s first district.** [**If you believe that’s what we need in Washington right now, please consider splitting a donation between my campaign and Eileen Laubacher's.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124216630/597927302/-1420152198?refcode=20260128-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTgxNzIiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZjFjMDdlOTMtN2JmYy1mMDExLThkNGMtMDAyMjQ4MmQyNzliIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=EmyGS0kescAO3CwffosHvANiUN6YicUnCREqzp5dgsc=)
The day I was removed from my position, I was forced to leave behind my life’s work. I never went back to the Pentagon or wore the uniform again.
But this story isn’t just about me. Throughout the first year of Donald Trump’s second term, every woman serving as a three or four-star admiral in the Navy has been fired, forced out, or reassigned. This wasn’t an isolated incident. It’s a pattern.
When leadership decisions are driven by politics instead of integrity, our families, communities, and nation pay the price.
**That’s why I’m running for Congress:** to keep serving, to stand up when it’s hardest, and to fight for leadership that puts country over politics every time.
[**Early support in races like this matters most. We have a long road ahead of us if we’re going to fill this open seat and make the government work for the people again. If you can, please split a donation between my campaign and Eileen Laubacher's to help me hit the ground running and prove that service to our country shouldn’t end just because someone in power says it should.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124216637/597927308/-1420152198?refcode=20260128-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTgxNzIiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZjFjMDdlOTMtN2JmYy1mMDExLThkNGMtMDAyMjQ4MmQyNzliIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=EmyGS0kescAO3CwffosHvANiUN6YicUnCREqzp5dgsc=)
With my deepest respect and gratitude,
Nancy Lacore
_Democratic Candidate for Congress
South Carolina’s First District_

I know how to defeat Sacramento, but I need your help launching this campaign.5 files Hi there Peter, This is Michael Gates - there's something I want to share, if you have 30 seconds. Most attorneys spend their entire careers trying to get to Washington, D.C. I was there. I was serving in the Trump Department of Justice, fighting for election integrity on the national stage. I even recently sued the State of California and Orange County to enforce federal election integrity laws. I was exactly where I thought I needed to be, doing work that mattered. But there was one problem: I was watching from a distance as my home state was destroyed. I saw the crime waves, the "woke" mandates, and the complete abandonment of the rule of law and our State and federal Constitutions. So I packed my bags and came home to the front lines. It was a difficult decision. People told me I was crazy (some still do!). But I know something they don't. I know they can be beaten. How? Because I 've actually done it as City Attorney for Huntington Beach for a decade: When they closed our beaches during COVID, we sued! Newsom had to reopen them. When they declared a "Sanctuary State," we fought Bonta in court. A judge ruled in our favor. When they tried to ban our new Voter ID law in Huntington Beach, Bonta sued us. We won. When the State passed AB 1955 mandating that teachers keep secrets from parents concerning their children's gender issues, we sued! But I'd be lying if I said fundraising doesn't make a difference in a race like this. The far-Left is readying a FORTUNE to drown out our message and protect their power. DemocracyDocket: SCOTUS to Hear GOP Lawsuit That Could Radically Restrict Mail Voting [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=012826_2&amount=25]
Team: Mail-in ballots are under attack again.
The Supreme Court agreed to hear arguments in RNC v. Wetzel, a lawsuit challenging Mississippi’s law allowing a five-day grace period for late-arriving ballots mailed by Election Day. In simpler terms, it's a case about whether your vote will count if you mail it on or before Election Day, but your ballot arrives after Election Day.
It's clear why a political party -- in this case, the Republican National Committee (RNC) -- is claiming that states must reject ballots that arrive after Election Day. Doing so would potentially disenfranchise a large number of voters, restricting the number of participants in an election. And the data is clear, over the last several election cycles, Republicans have been outnumbered in the use of mail-in ballots.
The RNC is making a blunt decision that their ability to win elections matters more than your vote. It's a cynical attempt to stay in power by suppressing ballots that are delivered late by the postal service. It's the kind of partisan work that shows they'd rather believe in their own power and control than the principles of democracy, of a country where all our votes should count, regardless of party.

Our position is clear: If your ballot was postmarked by Election Day, it should count.
This shouldn't be a partisan question. No political party -- Democrat, Republican, Green, Working Families, Libertarian, Reform, Conservative -- should be against voting. No party in our democracy should want to restrict the fundamental right of our fellow citizens to make their voice heard through voting.
But now we're facing a case where the Supreme Court’s decision could strike down or uphold laws in 16 states (and Washington D.C.) allowing late-arriving ballots postmarked on or before Election Day to be counted if they arrive within a set grace period.
How do we know what is at stake? Data from the 2024 Massachusetts elections shows that their three-day grace period for ballots to arrive after Election Day resulted in a 60% drop in rejected ballots as compared to no grace period. That means thousands of votes still counted, more than 1.5% of the total vote count. In a close election, that 1.5% could easily mean the difference between winning and losing.
Our fundamental right to vote should matter so much more than a partisan desperation to win. Chip in $35 or whatever you can to help us defend the use of mail-in ballots and make every vote count in elections nationwide >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=012826_2&amount=35]

name: Marie Gluesenkamp Perez
subject: Healthcare shouldn’t be this hard
body:
| | Peter,

Everywhere I go in Southwest Washington, I hear from folks concerned about the rising cost of healthcare.

Nearly 25,000 people in our district have seen their premiums jump since the enhanced ACA subsidies expired at the end of last year. I voted to extend those subsidies for three more years to give families some relief – but I also know temporary fixes aren’t enough.

Before I ever ran for Congress, my husband and I faced these same tradeoffs. We could only afford health insurance for our son. We went without coverage ourselves and hoped nothing would go wrong. No family should have to make that kind of choice.

Healthcare costs are squeezing people from every direction – premiums, deductibles, prescriptions – and it’s forcing real sacrifices. We need real reforms, not short-term patches, that lower costs, increase competition, and bring transparency to the system.

**That’s why I need to hear directly from you. Have your healthcare costs gone up? Are higher premiums or prescription prices forcing tough choices for your family or your business?** [Please take a moment to share your experience in this short survey:](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124218426/597932282/-618666345?refcode=MGP_EM_SV_90DO_260128_1_1&refcode2=fd8f9bf0-7dfc-f011-8d4c-0022482d279b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTkyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmZDhmOWJmMC03ZGZjLWYwMTEtOGQ0Yy0wMDIyNDgyZDI3OWIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ksqzjGa29AZXNsfC9o5vaHCfZXOFfxIIxJNsLehoyiA=&emci=ee8f9bf0-7dfc-f011-8d4c-0022482d279b&emdi=fd8f9bf0-7dfc-f011-8d4c-0022482d279b&ceid=31138575)

Healthcare isn’t just about insurance plans and paperwork. It’s about whether people can pay their bills and still afford to buy groceries and spend time with their kids, and whether they can stay healthy enough to keep showing up to work and life.

Your voice matters in shaping what I fight for next. Thank you for taking the time to share your story.

– Marie

Peter,
Janet Mills just entered the race against Susan Collins. So you’re about to get a million fundraising texts and emails from Mills and her campaign (if you haven’t already).
I’m new to this whole politics thing, but I’ve begun to learn how this works: After you donate to any establishment Democrat, Chuck Schumer and the DNC turn around and use your email address and phone number to put their thumbs on the scale – propping up their choice, even when that person is not the strongest candidate in the race.
It’s all part of the corrupt system in Washington. Corporations buy candidates through corporate PAC checks. Special interest groups like AIPAC pour millions into Super PACs. And Chuck Schumer and the DNC buy loyalty by sending millions of texts and emails to funnel money to milquetoast candidates, even when they don’t have the best chance to win.
I’m not the choice of corporations, AIPAC, Chuck Schumer, or the DNC. And that’s exactly why I’m the Democrat who is finally going to actually defeat Susan Collins and turn Maine blue.
Susan Collins is the most vulnerable Republican senator in the country. We have an opportunity to replace her with a Democrat who will actually support Medicare for All and call what’s happened in Gaza a genocide.
But I’m going up against Susan Collins, AIPAC, and the entire DC establishment. If I’m going to be able to defeat Susan Collins and flip this Senate seat blue, I am counting on folks like you to chip in now to our campaign.
Please, will you split a donation right now between my campaign and The Real Texas PAC to help me defeat Susan Collins, flip Maine blue, and take back the Senate for Democrats? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rtp-2025-platner?refcode=012726_2]

| Friends,

America is entering a new chapter in how we think about food and health.

With the release of the new federal nutrition guidelines, there’s growing recognition that the old model of counting calories, fearing protein, and chasing food trends has failed too many people.

What’s been missing from this conversation is muscle.

**Muscle isn’t just about strength or appearance. It’s the foundation of metabolic health, resilience as we age, and long-term independence.** And yet for decades, it’s been overlooked in our national approach to nutrition and wellness.

_That’s why I wrote The Forever Strong Playbook._

[ ](https://links.iterable.com/s/c/z9TX1YVN100YmFbBWDbZmvyEQq3j94Oo-7n6LZofvly_UktFuI5h4GPtzkOkv4gtxjEy0fBM05iFSqrdv2xppWMYZ5SFQACazM_oRMdCi3frzUVCIYcXvgQ-vDbsKpSbM5iVWZwMehw0J27akSpn6209r6mcFvkFK5rN8O77A7ltZ-P6BPhYY32cUj-nVPMSJtYkZD4M0fE9efcQCSJ7qCUnDyy0IyzJlU0bowFBvtbQzHcDDVOsn3ddnbunRS7j2Lg8op48ps54skNdIOtbwIuY1IEDW6kJMpphlGxZvoV_uwZOukv0JTvHKnEF3hTxpdhiON4SrHaJ7x0Yo-3MB803P1dla-qqYY939KGvgNj6k3ACcj3epqxuzdK_3ZWS0bLDRH3LcmLLlsAr3CFshPYZxzPWLQ2xgA/W72W1ql4YULDm6NN8D-rqloqtY-66XaH/17)

This book is about learning how to fuel your body properly through protein, strength training, and smart nutrition so you can protect your health, stay capable, and remain strong for decades to come. It’s designed to be practical, science-based, and realistic for real life.

As policymakers rethink how nutrition guidance should serve Americans, I want individuals and families to have the tools they need right now; tools that go beyond trends and focus on what truly works.

clean_body: | Friends, America is entering a new chapter in how we think about food and health. With the release of the new federal nutrition guidelines, there’s growing recognition that the old model of counting calories, fearing protein, and chasing food trends has failed too many people. What’s been missing from this conversation is muscle. Muscle isn’t just about strength or appearance. It’s the foundation of metabolic health, resilience as we age, and long-term independence. And yet for decades, it’s been overlooked in our national approach to nutrition and wellness. That’s why I wrote The Forever Strong Playbook. This book is about learning how to fuel your body properly through protein, strength training, and smart nutrition so you can protect your health, stay capable, and remain strong for decades to come. It’s designed to be practical, science-based, and realistic for real life. As policymakers rethink how nutrition guidance should serve Americans, I want individuals and families to have the tools they need right now; tools that go beyond trends and focus on what truly works. body:
Reintroducing myself.
#

Hey friend, it’s Mark Kelly. My friend Roy Cooper is running for Senate in North Carolina and needs our help. I hope you’ll read the message below from him, and [**rush a split donation between Roy's campaign and mine.**](https://act.markkelly.com/go/1389?c0=mek-em-cooper.oMEak6&refcode=em260128-1-30&t=1&akid=6346%2E6688874%2Eg4MDeR)
---
Hi Friend,
_I’m Roy Cooper. I'm running to be the next U.S. Senator from North Carolina, the most-likely Senate seat to flip. And together, we’re going to win._
You may know this about me already, but before I ask for your financial support ahead of my January fundraising deadline, I want to take a moment to reintroduce myself and remind you why I’m in this race — and why I’m counting on you to be in it with me.
[**__If you don’t need to read more, you can go ahead and split a donation between our campaign and Mark Kelly now.__**](https://act.markkelly.com/go/1389?c0=mek-em-cooper.oMEak6&refcode=em260128-1-30&t=2&akid=6346%2E6688874%2Eg4MDeR)
[](https://act.markkelly.com/go/1389?c0=mek-em-cooper.oMEak6&refcode=em260128-1-30&t=3&akid=6346%2E6688874%2Eg4MDeR)
I’m a proud father and husband. I’m a lifelong North Carolinian. The Carolina Hurricanes’ #1 fan. And I was honored to serve North Carolina as Governor, Attorney General, and a legislator.
🩺 During my time in office, I fought hard to expand Medicaid. It wasn’t easy — it took nearly a decade of advocacy, negotiation, and perseverance — but we got it done. And it brought 700,000 North Carolinians access to the care they need.
♻️ I helped build North Carolina’s clean energy economy, which brought good jobs to our communities while helping protect our environment for future generations.
♀️ Over and over, I used every power at my disposal to try to defend reproductive health care access from the far-right’s cruel, dangerous, anti-freedom abortion bans.
Look, this state is my home. I wanted to serve North Carolina and our communities from right here — I didn’t plan on trying to go to Washington. But when I look at what’s happening in this country today, I know I can’t leave things as they are for my children, or for yours.
I’m running for the U.S. Senate because I’m fed up with seeing extreme politicians strip away our rights, drive up the cost of living, tear apart our democracy and gut health care and SNAP benefits for folks in need. I’m ready for the fight, and I’m ready to deliver for the people. But I can’t get to Washington without your help. [**__We have a $500,000 online fundraising goal to meet this month, and falling behind might give the GOP the momentum they need to surge ahead. Please split anything you can between our campaign and Mark Kelly before our January deadline to close the gap.**__](https://act.markkelly.com/go/1389?c0=mek-em-cooper.oMEak6&refcode=em260128-1-30&t=4&akid=6346%2E6688874%2Eg4MDeR)

subject: We need to Abolish ICE (the bare minimum)
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY HEIDI HALL FOR CONGRESS
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/hall-email?refcode=20260128_em_fr_b1_HH_BIG [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/hall-email?refcode=20260128_em_fr_b1_HH_BIG]
Friend,
ICE isn't making our communities safer, and what we've seen in Minnesota makes it clear that this is far more than "a few bad apples" acting out—the entire tree is rotten.
This is an organization built on leveraging their status as a federal agency to commit murder and unconstitutionally brutalize our communities .
Abolishing ICE is now the bare minimum.
Anyone who can't see that, like our Republican opponent who just voted to fund the DHS , is either willfully ignorant or knowingly playing toxic political games with our lives.
Friend, I'm calling for the impeachment of Sec. Noem and trials for everyone involved in cases of ICE and CBP's criminal activity because we need to meet the dire moment that we're in with the necessary action.
I'm running for Congress because as a proven problem-solver, I know that words can only go so far, and our communities have heard enough. We need results.
Grassroots support has shown us that campaigns like ours, that understand rural and suburban communities, can go toe-to-toe with establishment figures and has proven that races like this belong to the people, not just those who’ve held office the longest.
With our January End of Month Fundraising Deadline coming up fast, we need your help to raise the $9,332 more we need to stay on track to flip this seat. Will you join us by donating any amount today? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/hall-email?refcode=20260128_em_fr_b1_HH_BIG]

Heidi Hall
Heidi Hall has spent her three-decade public service career working with others to solve problems, protect our land and water, improve health, and build opportunities for others, all while raising two boys primarily as a single mom.

Raised by parents who had persisted to make a middle-class life for their kids in Contra Costa County while lifting up others, Heidi was taught to push through and overcome challenges rather than complain about them. She learned to stick up for the vulnerable, to respect working people, and to value equal opportunity and justice.
After graduating from Pomona College and earning graduate degrees from Columbia and Rutgers, Heidi went to work for the Rockefeller Foundation promoting reproductive care and then began her career at the Environmental Protection Agency, stopping the dumping of toxic waste and holding corporate polluters accountable.
Today, Heidi chairs the Nevada County Board of Supervisors, where she’s taken on homelessness, expanded broadband access, and worked to reduce crime and illegal cannabis growth. Heidi flipped her seat from red to blue – and now she’s ready to do it again in Congress to take on toxic politics in Washington and put people first.

Dear firstname/friend,
I’m honored to share that my first bill to become a law as a Congresswoman will help veterans. The FAST VETS Act was signed into law this week, and it’s also the very first bill passed by a Democrat freshman in my class to become a law. It’s a bill I wrote to help servicemembers successfully transition into civilian life and find meaningful work after their service.
This is a real step forward in keeping our promise to America’s veterans.
For too many servicemembers, the battle continues long after they hang up their uniform. Without the right support, veterans face barriers to employment, stability, and opportunity, despite everything they have already given to this country.
I’ve seen these challenges up close. For seven years, I cared for veterans in VA hospitals and witnessed firsthand how critical strong transition and career support can be. The FAST VETS Act expands access to these programs, helping more veterans build stable, fulfilling lives after their term of service.
As a freshman member of Congress in the minority party, it is very challenging to get a bill passed into law. I am deeply grateful to have an amazing team that helped me get this done, despite the dysfunction in D.C. Our nation’s heroes will be assisted by this bill, and my commitment is to keep fighting for our veterans in every way we can.
We can’t slow down now. If you believe in keeping our promises to those who served, please chip in $5 today to help us keep fighting for veterans and pass the policies they deserve. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_med_email-26q1?refcode=x_260128_FASTVets_act&amount=5]

| | Friend, Ryan Binkley here – businessman, pastor, and your candidate for Congress in Texas's 32nd District.I’m reaching out to you personally because this issue matters deeply to every American family, including yours and mine. I want to speak straight from the heart about border security, ICE, and why we must get this right – now more than ever.
---
---
Let me be crystal clear: **I have never supported amnesty, and I never will.** Not under any circumstances. For too long, we've watched weak leadership allow our southern border to become a wide-open gateway, with devastating consequences for our communities, our economy, and our national security. Under Joe Biden’s reckless policies, **millions upon millions of illegal immigrants** have flooded into our country unchecked. This isn't just a statistic – it's a crisis that's driving down wages for hardworking American workers, overwhelming our schools and hospitals, straining local resources, and yes, putting American families at real risk with increased crime and fentanyl pouring across the border. President Trump proved what strong leadership looks like. He took decisive action to secure the border, built hundreds of miles of wall, implemented Remain in Mexico, and stood firmly with our brave men and women in **Border Patrol** and **ICE**. Those efforts worked – crossings plummeted, and America is safer and stronger. We cannot afford any half-measures or political games. We must **finish the job** that President Trump started.Here’s what I will fight for in Congress:
---
* **Full support for ICE and Border Patrol** – giving them the tools, funding, and backing they need to do their jobs without interference from radical politicians in Washington.
* **Mass deportations** of those here illegally, starting with criminals, gang members, and those who pose a threat to our communities.
* **A permanent, Trump-style border security plan** – including physical barriers where needed, advanced technology, more personnel, and policies that deter future illegal crossings for decades to come.
* **No temporary fixes, no compromises with the radical left** , and absolutely no surrender on America's sovereignty. We will never allow this invasion to happen again.

---
As a successful businessman who has spent years fixing broken systems and turning around companies, I know how to get results. I’ve built businesses from the ground up, balanced budgets, and delivered real outcomes, the same proven approach I’ll bring to Washington to secure our border, restore our economy, protect American jobs, and defend the rule of law. America must always come first. Our workers, our families, our children deserve leaders who will fight for them without apology. That’s why I’m running: to stand shoulder-to-shoulder with President Trump and deliver the strong, common-sense solutions our country needs. I’m asking for your support in the Republican primary on **March 3rd, and you can cast your vote early beginning February 17th.** Your vote will help send a clear message that Texans – and Americans – demand a secure border and a return to law and order.Together, we can protect our communities, support our heroes in law enforcement, and make sure America remains the greatest, safest nation on earth. Thank you for taking the time to read this. I’m grateful for your consideration and your patriotism.For a stronger, more secure America,**Ryan Binkley**
_Candidate for U.S. Congress – Texas District 32_
_Proud Supporter of President Trump_

Peter, They say hope for the best and plan for the worst. And our team here at the NDRC does just that. Shortly after the 2020 redistricting process concluded, we began preparing for a worst-case, far-fetched scenario: That Republicans might not wait until after the next census to start redrawing their maps in order to pick up congressional seats. Last summer, that worst-case scenario started coming true. And thanks to people like you, we were ready to respond with the full force of the fair maps movement. Your support has enabled us to push back against every Republican gerrymander and expose the craven politicians who’ve kowtowed to Trump’s demands. Supporters like you have helped us counteract these power grabs by giving voters in states like California a chance to pass temporary, responsive measures to prevent Republicans from rigging the outcome of the midterm elections. **The next few months will be the toughest test we’ve faced yet — and we’re prepared to respond with the urgency this moment demands. That’s why I’m calling on you, if you can, to step up with a grassroots donation. ** [**Donate to power the NDRC’s democracy-defending work in the critical months ahead, and ensure we’re ready no matter what attacks lie before us.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124221917/597942404/1128139581?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_HolderBehindScenes_email_20260128-NDRC-Tier1-HolderBehindScenes_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260128-NDRC-Tier1-HolderBehindScenes_&utm_campaign=HolderBehindScenes&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImI0YzVkNWY2LTgzZmMtZjAxMS04ZDRjLTAwMjI0ODJkMjc5YiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=K59HuiwzIIZ256-vrrHW7zDLs1cMcb2talBmed4sWJ4=) | _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_
