When Donald Trump got elected a second time, we knew that this redistricting crisis could be imminent — so we wasted no time. We knew that we couldn’t sit on the sidelines while Trump and his allies tried to rig voting maps and disenfranchise voters. We knew we couldn’t simply respond with strongly worded press statements.
We knew we had to respond with a massive organizing effort and make clear that the American people strongly rejected this power grab. And time and again, we’ve proven that organizing and fighting back _works_ — from the citizen-led effort in Missouri to give voters a chance to veto their gerrymandered map to the bipartisan coalition of Indiana lawmakers who resisted Trump’s pressure and voted down the attempted gerrymander there.
[**We don’t know what the future holds, but you can feel confident that your donation helps the NDRC prepare — even for a worst-case scenario. If you can, give today to power our movement and let’s fight for a truly fair, truly representative democracy.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124221939/597942427/1128139581?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_HolderBehindScenes_email_20260128-NDRC-Tier1-HolderBehindScenes_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260128-NDRC-Tier1-HolderBehindScenes_&utm_campaign=HolderBehindScenes&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImI0YzVkNWY2LTgzZmMtZjAxMS04ZDRjLTAwMjI0ODJkMjc5YiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=K59HuiwzIIZ256-vrrHW7zDLs1cMcb2talBmed4sWJ4=)
These are serious, consequential times. It is not hyperbolic to say that our democracy is at risk, that the American Experiment is in danger of destruction by zealots and authoritarians. We need your help. Together, we will prevail.
Thank you,
Eric H. Holder, Jr.

name: Ro Khanna
subject: Democrats must unite to defend the rule of law against ICE
body:
ICE has become a rogue, militarized police force on behalf of the Trump administration.
#
**I just returned from Minneapolis to thank protestors for standing up for our freedoms and to learn more about what’s happening firsthand.**
ICE has become a rogue, militarized police force on behalf of the Trump administration. They are coming after all of us—immigrants and American citizens alike—terrorizing our communities through physical assault, kidnapping, and even murder.
Congress has the power to stop this. Democrats must do everything they can to restore and defend the rule of law. **That’s why Carlos Eduardo Espina and I are rolling out a 10-point plan to hold ICE accountable and reform immigration enforcement:**
✅ Vote no on the DHS funding bill.
✅ Repeal the multi-year $75 billion funding for ICE.
✅ Impeach Noem and Bondi.
✅ End qualified immunity for ICE agents.
✅ Investigate and prosecute every single ICE agent who broke the law.
✅ End the Kavanaugh stops with racial profiling and the militarization of ICE.
✅ Codify a use-of-force standard so courts can enforce the law against rogue ICE agents.
✅ Tear down and replace ICE with an agency that has oversight.
✅ Prohibit masks and mandate body cameras and visible identification for immigration officers.
✅ Establish human rights standards at immigration detention facilities.
[**ADD YOUR NAME: Support my 10-point plan to address ICE’s abuse of power.**](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22272?t=1&akid=1483%2E2118727%2EDipf86)
**[SIGN THE PETITION](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22272?t=2&akid=1483%2E2118727%2EDipf86)**
The time for talking is over—we need action. Democrats must unite around this plan and stand up to Trump’s lawless administration.
Thank you for your activism and all that you do.
In solidarity,
Ro
* * *
**Wait! One more thing–** Ro doesn't accept a cent from lobbyists or PACs, meaning our work is completely funded by grassroots supporters like you. By donating just $3 today, you’re helping us create a country that works for everyone, not just those at the top. That means a renewed investment in American manufacturing, Medicare for All, student debt relief, and a green future. If you want to support our people-powered campaign as we continue to fight for progress in Washington, please consider making a donation of $3 or more today. Thank you! **[DONATE $3](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22273?c0=leftnet_em20260128.1fa_F0&refcode=em20260128-1483&t=3&akid=1483%2E2118727%2EDipf86)** **[DONATE MORE](https://act.leftnet.org/go/21450?c0=leftnet_em20260128.CszEsG&refcode=em20260128-1483&t=4&akid=1483%2E2118727%2EDipf86)**

body:
By now you've no doubt read the news about Alex Pretti and Reneé Nicole Good, two American citizens shot and killed by federal law enforcement officials in Minneapolis.
#

Team,
By now you've no doubt read the news about Alex Pretti and Renée Nicole Good, two American citizens shot and killed by federal law enforcement officials in Minneapolis. These killings continue a larger pattern of violence from ICE, which we’ve seen across the country.
Here is the truth:
This tragedy deserves a full, transparent investigation, and ICE needs to get out of Minnesota. ICE surges in places like Minnesota do not increase public safety — they erode safety, escalate violence, and stoke fear in communities.
As you may have also heard, Alex Pretti was carrying a gun and had a legal permit to do so when he was shot.
As a general rule, the data and research tells us that more guns in public do not make people safer. Period. But in this instance, Alex Pretti had a concealed carry permit and was following the law.
For years and years, many on the far-right have peddled the dangerous notion that everyone carrying guns at all times will make the world a safer place.
Today, you're seeing politicians on the right blaming Alex Pretti for his own murder because he was carrying a gun. That is incredibly dangerous for millions of Americans. We're hearing from a lot of responsible gun owners about this and we understand their concern.
So where do we go from here?
Like we said, ICE needs to get out of Minnesota. There needs to be an investigation into these shootings. And at GIFFORDS, we will continue to work every day to make our communities safer from gun violence: whether those are mass shootings, self-inflicted gun violence, domestic violence, political violence, and instances like this in Minnesota as well.
But we can't do that alone:

the United States 7-2 decision in favor of granting standing in a
historic case filed on behalf of Congressman Mike Bost and two
presidential electors, who were before the court to vindicate their
standing to challenge an Illinois law allowing the counting of
ballots received up to 14 days after Election Day.

Hi, We’re less than a week away from wrapping up January, and the urgency of holding the Trump administration accountable is crystal clear. Families are in limbo over healthcare access. The cost of groceries, rent, and basic necessities continues to rise. And the Trump administration fuels more division by the day. Before we get further into the year — and inevitably caught up responding to the next crisis — I want to pause and hear directly from you about the issues that matter most to you in 2026. The son of hardworking farmworkers, Dr. Ruiz grew up in Coachella, CA and learned at an early age that the key to attaining the American Dream is hard work and a great education. In the summer of 1990, Raul walked in the desert heat from business to business in the Coachella Valley asking them to invest in their community by contributing to his education. With each investment for college, he made a promise to come back home and serve his community as a physician. In 2012, he decided to take his service to the community to the next level by running for Congress. **Dr. Ruiz needs our help to continue fighting for us in Congress.**

Demand Congress protect our country against unimaginable hardship 📩 | | | Peter, what happens if DACA ends? This is the question that hundreds of thousands of DACA recipients have been asking themselves for years, as members of Congress fail to deliver permanent protections for our communities. For thirteen years, DACA has allowed immigrant youth to build their families, careers, and businesses in the U.S. DACA recipients are part of the fabric of our communities — they teach our children, care for our loved ones, and contribute billions to our economy every year. We have organized relentlessly to ensure DACA recipients and immigrant youth can continue living in safety and dignity in the only home they’ve ever known. But with immigration agents violating DACA protections and detaining DACA recipients, every single one of us will need to speak out to protect the safety and stability of our neighbors. **When immigrants are attacked, we**** _all_****pay the price. If DACA ended tomorrow, our communities would face unimaginable economic harm:**
* 💼 Our country would lose 1,000 jobs every single business day for the next two years — that’s nearly 500,000 jobs lost!
* 🏥 At least 18,000 jobs would be lost every month, including 1,500 healthcare workers, 700 teachers and educators, and 600 personal care workers who help our communities thrive
* 👪 At least 13,000 US citizen children would be at risk of losing their parent to detention and deportation

clean_body: Demand Congress protect our country against unimaginable hardship 📩 | | | Peter, what happens if DACA ends? This is the question that hundreds of thousands of DACA recipients have been asking themselves for years, as members of Congress fail to deliver permanent protections for our communities. For thirteen years, DACA has allowed immigrant youth to build their families, careers, and businesses in the U.S. DACA recipients are part of the fabric of our communities — they teach our children, care for our loved ones, and contribute billions to our economy every year. We have organized relentlessly to ensure DACA recipients and immigrant youth can continue living in safety and dignity in the only home they’ve ever known. But with immigration agents violating DACA protections and detaining DACA recipients, every single one of us will need to speak out to protect the safety and stability of our neighbors. When immigrants are attacked, we allpay the price. If DACA ended tomorrow, our communities would face unimaginable economic harm: 💼 Our country would lose 1,000 jobs every single business day for the next two years — that’s nearly 500,000 jobs lost! 🏥 At least 18,000 jobs would be lost every month, including 1,500 healthcare workers, 700 teachers and educators, and 600 personal care workers who help our communities thrive 👪 At least 13,000 US citizen children would be at risk of losing their parent to detention and deportation Can we count on you and your community to join us in advocating for permanent protections for our immigrant neighbors? 🤳Share our latest video with your friends and family today: Can you grow your impact today and demand Congress deliver permanent protections and end the detention of DACA recipients currently missing from our communities? # **McMaster’s final State of the State address + Democrat Jermaine Johnson Responds**
# **Wednesday at 7pm**
---
|
---
| |
On Wednesday evening,**** Governor McMaster will deliver his final State of the State address to the General Assembly. Immediately following his remarks, **state Representative and Democratic Candidate for Governor, Jermaine Johnson will lead the Democratic response** to the governor’s speech.
You'll be able to watch the Democratic response to the State of the State [**live on SCETV**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=56e4f584a0&e=edbde6c9b1) as well as our [**SC House Democrats**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=9c88bd081a&e=edbde6c9b1) social media pages.

This past week, there were hearings for top priorities of the Republican supermajority, including:
[**H. 4756**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=ccccb0b82f&e=edbde6c9b1)**, “the bathroom bill.”** Republicans are very concerned about who can use which bathroom. This bill requires a person to use the restroom of the gender they were assigned at birth. The consequence of this bill: you’ll have people who have undergone gender transition in the wrong bathroom – that is, grown men with big beards in the same bathroom as little girls. How will this bill be enforced? Will someone inspect your private parts before you can go to the bathroom? Maybe [**TSA can set up security checkpoints outside every toilet stall**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=12661ed3a6&e=edbde6c9b1).
This bill was passed by the Judiciary Committee on Tuesday, so you can expect the debate on the House floor as soon as next week for the first “Wicked Wednesday” of the year.
[**H. 3643**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=b03211e99e&e=edbde6c9b1)**and**[**H. 3310**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=ed6be8d011&e=edbde6c9b1) , which are two competing versions of the same idea: **establishing closed primary elections** by requiring you to register as a member of a political party in order to vote in that party’s primary. Under current South Carolina law, voters do _not_ register with a party, so voters can choose to participate in either party’s primary elections. Voter turnout in primaries is already very low – and these proposals would further reduce the number of people who participate. With fewer moderates and independents voting, that means more and more extreme candidates will win Republican primary elections... Have I mentioned that [**you should run for office?**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=6f2c472f12&e=edbde6c9b1)
These bills were _not_ passed out of subcommittee on Wednesday. As one bill is backed by the Republican establishment and the other bill is backed by the far right “Freedom” Caucus, I’ll be sure to keep you updated on their infighting.
[**H. 4760**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=c69f8c54ba&e=edbde6c9b1)**, a ban on medication abortion**. If it’s January at the South Carolina State House, that means Republicans are pushing yet another abortion ban – even though our abortion ban law is one of the strictest in the country. This is an attack on women’s freedom to make their own medical decisions and this bill is especially egregious because it will prevent survivors of rape and incest – who have up to 12 weeks to get an abortion under current law – from getting the safe, discrete care that they need. Additionally, it will restrict access to medications that are prescribed to treat conditions like high blood sugar, stomach ulcers, arthritis and more.
The new abortion ban was passed Wednesday evening by the Judiciary Committee, so expect to see it on the House floor soon – and you can count on House Democrats to fight back. - From the desk of **Nick Sottile, SC House Democrats**

# **My remarks from the Commissioner of Public Works Meeting**
---
| | Yesterday, Dr. Octavia Amaechi was sworn in as the Commissioner of Public Works in Spartanburg. She won 60% of the vote and made history as the first black women to be elected city-wide, and the first public health official to serve on the commission. But instead of being sworn in last month, her opponent, who works for the same development firm as the other commissioner of public works, was appointed to a vacant seat before she was sworn in. They have now set a dangerous precedent for future elections, further eroding the public’s trust in our largest public utility, and in my humble opinion should be forced to resign. [Read more here](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=e89be588df&e=edbde6c9b1).
---
| [Listen to Clemson Turregano’s testimony](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=e47ca72732&e=edbde6c9b1)
---
[|
---](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=f07725611d&e=edbde6c9b1)
| |

Good afternoon, my name is Kathryn Harvey. I am a citizen of the City of Spartanburg, and an owner of the Spartanburg water system.
I object to the appointment of Dillon Swayngim to the Commission of Public Works. The process of his appointment has created suspicion in the community.
I speak for myself, but also as someone who has been active in the local community for the last decade. People come to me with their concerns. The appointment of Dillon Swayngim is very concerning.
Voters had their say in November. Dr Amaechi received 14% more votes in the general election than Swayngim, and 21% more in the runoff. The message couldn't be clearer. Voters do not want Dillon Swayngim on the CPW, I believe largely due to the fact that he works for the same organization as Commissioner John Montgomery.
We, the people do not want two people who work for the same development company on a 3-person commission, especially since the work they do is directly impacted by decisions made regarding our water system.
Whenever 2 members of a 3 member commission are together, there is a quorum, and that meeting must be public. Even the best intended public servants who believe they are committed to never discussing CPW business in private cannot expect us to believe that this will not happen.
Why was Dr. Amaechi's swearing-in delayed until today, more than 2 months after she was elected to serve?
Outgoing commissioners Littlejohn and Viney were sworn in at December meetings. In fact, the Spartanburg water website had commissioner photos with captions stating their terms end in November of their outgoing years.
We are concerned that Swayngim’s appointment was made by Commissioners Montgomery and Littlejohn, at a special meeting convened less than 48 hours after the regular December 2025 meeting. Horace Littlejohn's term ended November 2025. Yet he voted at the regular December meeting and the special meeting.
Why was it so important to John Montgomery to have Horace Littlejohn's term extended beyond 6 years to January, in order to have John’s coworker sit on the commission giving Colliers two votes of the [three](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=19446db764&e=edbde6c9b1)? We have to be asking the question, why? What is coming down the pipeline?
We are still going through the repercussions of a sheriff's department with slippery ethics. We need no implication of corruption with the CPW.
We must think future-forward. Our county is under much development pressure. There are concerns about the new data centers and their need for water and the cost to us. A new Duke energy rate hike was just approved.
Be sure of this - we are going to hold all of our public servants accountable. At every meeting, and then again at the ballot box.
You work for us. This is a public utility, the most important public utility. We citizens intend to protect it and will challenge you at every turn, and keep the information about this wrongdoing, and about any decisions you make, front and center.
We deserve - we demand - open process, transparency, and good governance.
Thank you.

This past week we were back at the state house for hearings on a bill that would close our primaries and a bill that would ban abortion medication from being mailed to women in South Carolina who need it the most. This week the main bill is on bathrooms. If you want change at the state house then run for something, because we deserve better than this.
We were inspired by words from Revered Barber of the Poor People’s Campaign during MLK Weekend, hosted Rep Ro Khana in Spartanburg and knocked 200 doors to get voters energized ahead of the June 9 primaries.
Stay with me y’all, democracy is a participatory sport.

If it’s January at the South Carolina State House, that means Republicans are pushing yet another abortion ban – even though our abortion ban law is one of the strictest in the country. This is an attack on women’s freedom to make their own medical decisions and this bill is especially egregious because it will prevent survivors of rape and incest – who have up to 12 weeks to get an abortion under current law – from getting the safe, discrete care that they need. Additionally, it will restrict access to medications that are prescribed to treat conditions like high blood sugar, stomach ulcers, arthritis and more. The new abortion ban was passed Wednesday evening by the Judiciary Committee, so expect to see it on the House floor soon – and you can count on House Democrats to fight back. - From the desk of Nick Sottile, SC House Democrats | | | My remarks from the Commissioner of Public Works Meeting** | | Yesterday, Dr. Octavia Amaechi was sworn in as the Commissioner of Public Works in Spartanburg. She won 60% of the vote and made history as the first black women to be elected city-wide, and the first public health official to serve on the commission. But instead of being sworn in last month, her opponent, who works for the same development firm as the other commissioner of public works, was appointed to a vacant seat before she was sworn in. They have now set a dangerous precedent for future elections, further eroding the public’s trust in our largest public utility, and in my humble opinion should be forced to resign. . | | | Good afternoon, my name is Kathryn Harvey. I am a citizen of the City of Spartanburg, and an owner of the Spartanburg water system. I object to the appointment of Dillon Swayngim to the Commission of Public Works. The process of his appointment has created suspicion in the community. I speak for myself, but also as someone who has been active in the local community for the last decade. People come to me with their concerns. The appointment of Dillon Swayngim is very concerning. Voters had their say in November. Dr Amaechi received 14% more votes in the general election than Swayngim, and 21% more in the runoff. The message couldn't be clearer. Voters do not want Dillon Swayngim on the CPW, I believe largely due to the fact that he works for the same organization as Commissioner John Montgomery. We, the people do not want two people who work for the same development company on a 3-person commission, especially since the work they do is directly impacted by decisions made regarding our water system. Whenever 2 members of a 3 member commission are together, there is a quorum, and that meeting must be public. Even the best intended public servants who believe they are committed to never discussing CPW business in private cannot expect us to believe that this will not happen. Why was Dr. Amaechi's swearing-in delayed until today, more than 2 months after she was elected to serve? Outgoing commissioners Littlejohn and Viney were sworn in at December meetings. In fact, the Spartanburg water website had commissioner photos with captions stating their terms end in November of their outgoing years. We are concerned that Swayngim’s appointment was made by Commissioners Montgomery and Littlejohn, at a special meeting convened less than 48 hours after the regular December 2025 meeting. Horace Littlejohn's term ended November 2025. Yet he voted at the regular December meeting and the special meeting. Why was it so important to John Montgomery to have Horace Littlejohn's term extended beyond 6 years to January, in order to have John’s coworker sit on the commission giving Colliers two votes of the ? We have to be asking the question, why? What is coming down the pipeline? We are still going through the repercussions of a sheriff's department with slippery ethics. We need no implication of corruption with the CPW. We must think future-forward. Our county is under much development pressure. There are concerns about the new data centers and their need for water and the cost to us. A new Duke energy rate hike was just approved. Be sure of this - we are going to hold all of our public servants accountable. At every meeting, and then again at the ballot box. You work for us. This is a public utility, the most important public utility. We citizens intend to protect it and will challenge you at every turn, and keep the information about this wrongdoing, and about any decisions you make, front and center. We deserve - we demand - open process, transparency, and good governance. Thank you. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | This past week we were back at the state house for hearings on a bill that would close our primaries and a bill that would ban abortion medication from being mailed to women in South Carolina who need it the most. This week the main bill is on bathrooms. If you want change at the state house then run for something, because we deserve better than this. We were inspired by words from Revered Barber of the Poor People’s Campaign during MLK Weekend, hosted Rep Ro Khana in Spartanburg and knocked 200 doors to get voters energized ahead of the June 9 primaries. Stay with me y’all, democracy is a participatory sport. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Copyright (C) 2026 Kathryn for SC. All rights reserved.

| | Friend, I want to share something important. I’m honored to receive the official endorsement from **For The Future Victory Fund**. This matters not because of a logo or a name, but because it affirms what this campaign truly represents. **A fight for the future, not a defense of the past.** I’m running because **Lauren Boebert is not our future.**
**Donald Trump and his regime are not our future.** What they represent is **unsustainable**. It is built on revisionist history and a version of America that no longer exists. It cannot meet the challenges working families face today, and their destructive policies are **eroding our democratic institutions, weaponizing the federal government, and destabilizing our economy** by feeding more money to the top while **the working class collapses under pressure**. I’m running for **the future of our democracy**.
I’m running for **the future of our economy** , so working people can build stability instead of just surviving.
I’m running for **the future of our environment** , because protecting our water, land, and resources is essential to life in Colorado. This fight is personal. **I’m not just a dad. I’m a working-class dad who punches a clock, makes tradeoffs, and carries responsibility every single day.** I know what it’s like to make sacrifices so your kids don’t go without. I know what it’s like to live the reality that **nearly 70 percent of Americans face** , one paycheck away from financial ruin. I know the stress of rising healthcare premiums, impossible housing costs, student debt, and the feeling of **maxing out a credit card or zeroing out your checking account every time you go to the grocery store**. **I’ve lived it. And I refuse to accept that this is the best America can offer.** People are ready for **fighters**. People are ready for leaders who will **disrupt the status quo** , not offer more of the same **stale, watered down approaches** the political establishment has pushed on working families for decades. I’m running so **young people can afford to start their lives**.
So **retirees on fixed incomes can live with dignity and security**.
So **our military is strong, well paid, and protected** , and so we stop sending our sons and daughters into foreign conflicts that do not make us safer or serve a clear mission. **Every decision I make is guided by the future my children will inherit.** I’m fighting for them, and **I will fight for your family with the same love, grit, and determination I give my own.** ******You are my family.** This endorsement is a sign that **momentum is building**. People are ready for leadership that **understands struggle because it has lived it** , and that is willing to **fight forward instead of clinging to the past**. If you believe in building **a future worth passing on** , I’m asking you to stand with me by donating, volunteering, and showing up. **Together, we can build the future we need.** ******[This campaign is about our future. Hi Peter, As January wraps up, I wanted to share a thoughtful roundup of what we’ve been building across Wake County and why this work matters now more than ever.
* * *
**Wake County House Parties** Recently, we hosted another Wake County house party where neighbors dug into public safety, accountability, and why this race for Wake District Attorney matters. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124225014/597950628/1681264041?refcode=AU_GWN_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260128_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84ODMxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2NWJjNGY0Ni04YmZjLWYwMTEtOGQ0Yy0wMDIyNDgyZDI3OWIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Reb_dW7Y-DSF0XxIJw5RagZVYcGdcw1n2Ie91uJyYFk=) Thanks to newly-elected Cary Town Councilmember Brittany Richards for joining the conversation and to everyone who came ready to listen, ask hard questions, and push for common-sense solutions.
* * *
**Canvass Kickoff** Earlier this month, _more than 75 volunteers_ showed up in Cary to launch our canvassing effort. It was cold and rainy, and that turnout spoke volumes about the grit of this grassroots team. That kind of commitment is exactly how Democrats win and how we bring our positive message for change to voters across the county. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124225015/597950629/1681264041?refcode=AU_GWN_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260128_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84ODMxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2NWJjNGY0Ni04YmZjLWYwMTEtOGQ0Yy0wMDIyNDgyZDI3OWIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Reb_dW7Y-DSF0XxIJw5RagZVYcGdcw1n2Ie91uJyYFk=)
* * *
**Injustice anywhere is a threat to justice everywhere** I also had the honor of attending the 46th Annual Martin Luther King Jr. Ecumenical Service in Raleigh. Dr. King’s words stayed with me all week, _“An injustice anywhere is a threat to justice everywhere.”_ They’re a reminder that laws must be enforced with judgment, with compassion, and with respect for the dignity of every person. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124225016/597950630/1681264041?refcode=AU_GWN_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260128_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84ODMxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2NWJjNGY0Ni04YmZjLWYwMTEtOGQ0Yy0wMDIyNDgyZDI3OWIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Reb_dW7Y-DSF0XxIJw5RagZVYcGdcw1n2Ie91uJyYFk=)

subject: Abolish ICE
body:
Doris wants reform, Mai wants to Abolish ICE

| | | | | [|
---](https://maiforus.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fe5f60ccb8fb671f0c1857dc9&id=5123dc27b9&e=dd5af5b7b1)
| [ELECT A FIGHTER TO CONGRESS](https://maiforus.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fe5f60ccb8fb671f0c1857dc9&id=3ee3c32bb7&e=dd5af5b7b1)
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Dear ,
ICE just killed two people in Minnesota and nine people (_that we know of_) in 2026. ICE kidnaps children, steals people from their workplaces, breaks into homes without warrants, and cages people in inhumane conditions. The water is putrid. The food is rotten. People in detention are being denied lifesaving medical treatment. It’s not a time for statements. It’s time for action.
[**We need a representative who wants to ABOLISH ICE, not reform it. Donate now to unseat an Establishment Dem in CA-7 and get a Progressive to Congress.**](https://maiforus.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fe5f60ccb8fb671f0c1857dc9&id=131c1a3da0&e=dd5af5b7b1)
Councilmember Mai Vang has been protesting ICE for years. [Last night, she made a call for Sacramento to move from words to action and to protect our communities. ](https://maiforus.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fe5f60ccb8fb671f0c1857dc9&id=9499d5c0fd&e=dd5af5b7b1)
**“ICE must be abolished. Until then, Sacramento cannot afford to be reactive. We will protect each other.” – Councilmember Mai Vang**
While Representative Matsui makes statements and calls for tepid reforms to an inhumane agency, Councilmember Vang is:
---
| |
✅ Advancing a resolution prohibiting ICE on city property.
✅ Working with community organizers and colleagues calling on the City to develop the Sacramento Community Safety Action Plan in preparation for mass raids and militarized enforcement.
✅ Creating a child and family protection system — pre-identifying emergency caregivers, partnering with schools and community organizations.
✅ Allocating emergency funding for legal assistance and basic needs.
✅ Affirming Sacramento's commitment to protecting protesters — because standing up for our neighbors is not a crime.
---
| | [**[DONATE NOW to lift Mai Vang and progressive values from City Hall to the halls of Congress]**](https://maiforus.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fe5f60ccb8fb671f0c1857dc9&id=3fce47a24b&e=dd5af5b7b1)
As Congress stands idly by while ICE terrorizes our neighborhoods, we need a leader who shows courage. As a member of Congress, Mai will immediately work to abolish ICE and hold ICE agents and administration officials accountable. But she can’t do it alone.
As a City Councilmember, Mai Vang fights unapologetically for the working families of Sacramento. She rejects corporate PAC money; her people-powered campaign is completely grassroots funded. Join the movement today.
[**Will you pitch in $5, $10, or $25 now to elect Mai to Congress?**](https://maiforus.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fe5f60ccb8fb671f0c1857dc9&id=303656d4fc&e=dd5af5b7b1)
Sincerely,Team Mai

Friend, **Republicans spent thousands on attack ads against me in the last election, and I’m sure they will do the same this time. I need your help to fight back.** If that’s all you need to hear, you can use this link to chip in to my campaign to flip battleground AZ-01:**_[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/loc_mgw_fr_q12026](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124226193/597954699/-195036717?refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.01.28_Humbly_B1_F1_S1_C1_AC_N-T0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDYwODgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYjQzY2Y5NDAtOGRmYy1mMDExLThkNGMtMDAyMjQ4MmQyNzliIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=JrOR7OgGAdpMKaFIs4jli-ji4YOL8a4xSp_oPTrt1t8=)_** If not, let me explain to you how much your donation matters. Running for any seat in the House of Representatives is never easy — but this race is especially tough since AZ-01 is one of the most competitive House races in the country. To compete, we need to organize early, hire strong staff, reach voters online and on the ground, and make sure people hear the truth before MAGA defines this race for us. **That all takes resources.** I know fundraising emails are annoying. I’d much rather be out talking with voters and fighting for our values. But we must do both. name: Mohan Seshadri, API PA
subject: We demand: Stop funding ICE!
body:
https://www.apipennsylvania.org [https://www.apipennsylvania.org]
Hi Peter,
Yesterday, hundreds of Pennsylvanians gathered to protest at Senator Fetterman’s offices across the commonwealth, and made a clear demand: stop funding ICE.
While Congress is considering a budget bill that greatly increases funding for ICE, our communities are reeling from the violence committed by lawless masked agents in our neighborhoods. ICE has been acting without accountability to tear families apart, terrorize our communities, and threaten our freedoms. They have contributed to the deaths of dozens of our community members, whether in inhumane detention conditions or through reckless violence on the streets.
During times like these, showing up matters. In a powerful display of solidarity, protestors across Pennsylvania braved the cold to say NO MORE. From Philly to Pittsburgh, hundreds gathered at Senator Fetterman’s offices to demand Congress take action to protect all our communities, and stand against ICE’s deadly racism and xenophobia.
The fight isn’t over. Take action, and call Senator Fetterman’s office to demand no more money for ICE: (202) 224-4254

name: Ro Khanna
subject: TAKE ACTION: Hold ICE accountable
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Ro for Congress
body:
https://rokhanna.com [https://rokhanna.com]
Peter,
I visited Minneapolis this week to thank protesters fighting for our constitutional values and to hear firsthand what’s happening on the ground. Their stories prove just how lawless ICE has become. ICE agents are waiting outside people’s homes and following them in their cars. They’re tear-gassing neighborhoods. People are carrying their passports with them to avoid detainment, leaving their homes for days at a time when ICE is spotted in their neighborhoods, and delivering groceries to families terrified to venture outside.
WATCH: Minneapolis residents share their experiences with ICE [https://x.com/RoKhanna/status/2016568273786093806]
https://x.com/RoKhanna/status/2016568273786093806 [https://x.com/RoKhanna/status/2016568273786093806]
Congress has the power to stop this. Democrats must do everything they can to restore and defend the rule of law. That’s why Carlos Eduardo Espina and I are rolling out a 10-point plan to hold ICE accountable and reform immigration enforcement:
✅ Vote no on the DHS funding bill.
✅ Repeal the multi-year $75 billion funding for ICE.
✅ Impeach Noem and Bondi.
✅ End qualified immunity for ICE agents.
✅ Investigate and prosecute every single ICE agent who broke the law.
✅ End the Kavanaugh stops with racial profiling and the militarization of ICE.
✅ Codify a use-of-force standard so courts can enforce the law against rogue ICE agents.
✅ Tear down and replace ICE with an agency that has oversight.
✅ Prohibit masks and mandate body cameras and visible identification for immigration officers.
✅ Establish human rights standards at immigration detention facilities.

| | Hey friend, it's Deb Haaland. My friend Tim Walz is asking for our support of his Legal Defense Fund to fight back against the Justice Department's attacks. [Will you give him a moment to share why this is important, and then consider making a donation?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/4548?refcode=jtk231-bu-nd&t=2&akid=7144%2E400544%2EgAMf4s) Thank you. – Deb

Friend,

I wanted to emphasize just how serious of a moment we are in.

Donald Trump’s federal agents have been going door to door in Minnesota looking for folks based on their accent or color of their skin. Kids are afraid to go to school, small businesses are hurting, another life has been lost, and the people responsible have yet to be held accountable. Instead, Donald Trump’s DOJ is investigating me.
Why? Because my focus has always been protecting the people of Minnesota.
They’re trying to scare me and our state — but Minnesota will not be intimidated into silence and neither will I. This legal battle will be expensive, that’s why they’re doing this. They want me to back down and surrender, but I won’t.
[**I need your help in this fight. If you’re able, please split a donation between our Legal Defense Fund and Deb Haaland's campaign for governor and make sure we can continue to stand up to Donald Trump and his DOJ?**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/4548?refcode=jtk231-bu-nd&t=3&akid=7144%2E400544%2EgAMf4s)
I’m grateful,

Tim Walz

subject: I’m suing Pete Hegseth:
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Maggie for NH
body:
Donald Trump and Pete Hegseth want to use the power of the White House and the Department of Defense to silence me because they don’t like what I have to say.

Team, it's Mark.

**I am suing the Secretary of Defense.**

After 25 years in uniform and another 5 in the United States Senate, I never imagined I’d have to do something like this. Hegseth has left me no choice.

Donald Trump and Pete Hegseth want to use the power of the White House and the Department of Defense to punish me because they don’t like what I have to say. Their attacks are directed at me right now, but they’re trying to send a message to every retired member of the military:

Speak out against us and we will come after you with every tool we have at our disposal. We’ll censure you, we’ll threaten your rank and retirement, and we might even court-martial you.

It’s unconstitutional, so I’m suing them. Beyond this lawsuit, it’s important we send a message to Trump and Hegseth to show them just how many people are on this team to defend constitutional rights. That’s where you come in.

I’ve been truly humbled by the support people have sent my way over the past couple of months. It means the world to me that so many of you care about what Trump and Hegseth are trying to do.

That’s how we’ve made it this far, and it’s how we’ll get to the other side of this chapter in our nation’s history. Together.

If you’ve been waiting for the right time to make a stand and join the fight, this is it.

| | As Oregon’s Secretary of State and a member of the State Board of Education, I take our state’s K-12 education system extremely seriously. body:
Americans are at the breaking point.

| | | | | [|
---](https://chrisahuja.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=67424df89870d1cac00e55f46&id=779ff5cc7b&e=53c7d12fc7)
| | | | | | Dear Peter,Washington is trying to distract us, and working families can’t afford it.Every day, there’s a new headline meant to pull attention away: Greenland. Venezuela. Immigration raids. Political chaos designed by MAGA Republicans to distract and dominate the news cycle.In California’s 32nd District, the real crisis hasn’t changed.Rent is too high.Groceries cost more every week.Health care, child care, and gas are squeezing families who are already stretched thin.While Washington continues to create distractions with paramilitary forces and threats to sovereign nations and allies, working people are paying the price.I am running for Congress because affordability and economic security are not side issues, they are THE issues. And our concerns deserve to be heard.I believe Congress should be:• Lowering everyday costs for families• Protecting workers from corporate price-gouging• Strengthening access to affordable health care• Building an economy that works for people who earn a paycheck, not just those who profit from itDonald Trump’s economic legacy is clear: higher costs, weakened protections, and instability at home and abroad. Working families cannot afford more chaos disguised as leadership.In CA-32, we deserve better than Brad Sherman; absent, unresponsive, and out of touch with the daily realities of our communities. Leadership means listening, communicating, and showing up every time.Winning this race means rejecting distraction and demanding results. It means standing up to those who enable chaos and building a campaign rooted in local action and economic dignity.Donate today and join me in standing up for working families and prioritizing affordability over chaos. clean_body: Americans are at the breaking point. | | | | | | | | | | | Dear Peter,Washington is trying to distract us, and working families can’t afford it.Every day, there’s a new headline meant to pull attention away: Greenland. Venezuela. Immigration raids. Political chaos designed by MAGA Republicans to distract and dominate the news cycle.In California’s 32nd District, the real crisis hasn’t changed.Rent is too high.Groceries cost more every week.Health care, child care, and gas are squeezing families who are already stretched thin.While Washington continues to create distractions with paramilitary forces and threats to sovereign nations and allies, working people are paying the price.I am running for Congress because affordability and economic security are not side issues, they are THE issues. And our concerns deserve to be heard.I believe Congress should be:• Lowering everyday costs for families• Protecting workers from corporate price-gouging• Strengthening access to affordable health care• Building an economy that works for people who earn a paycheck, not just those who profit from itDonald Trump’s economic legacy is clear: higher costs, weakened protections, and instability at home and abroad. Working families cannot afford more chaos disguised as leadership.In CA-32, we deserve better than Brad Sherman; absent, unresponsive, and out of touch with the daily realities of our communities. Leadership means listening, communicating, and showing up every time.Winning this race means rejecting distraction and demanding results. It means standing up to those who enable chaos and building a campaign rooted in local action and economic dignity.Donate today and join me in standing up for working families and prioritizing affordability over chaos. name: Lizzie Fletcher
subject: Elections Matter - Especially This Saturday’s Election for TX-18
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS
body:
ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/82676/images/Non-Re-Elect%20Logo.png]
In recent days, I have heard from so many people distraught at what is happening in our country, worried for our future, and wondering what can be done.
If you live in Texas’ 18th Congressional District, there is one thing you can do right now: Vote. Today. (And if you don’t live there, call someone who does and help get out the vote.)
For nearly a year, Governor Abbott has denied the people who live in the 18th District in Houston their voice in Washington after the tragic death of my friend and colleague Congressman Sylvester Turner.
The people of the 18th Congressional District deserve better. And that is why I endorsed Christian Menefee in this race last March .
Christian is an original member of #TeamLizzie, going all the way back to the primary election in 2018. But that’s not why I endorsed him. I endorsed him because he is smart, thoughtful, and hardworking. And because he leads with integrity. As Harris County Attorney, Christian took on President Trump, Governor Abbott, and other Republican state officials to protect voting rights, defend health care, and fight for our civil rights. Time and again, he won many of those battles.
The people of the 18th Congressional District deserve a fighter who can get things done. And we need him in our Texas Delegation in Congress.
Here’s what you need to know about the election and the final GOTV push:
Early voting is happening right now!
* Wednesday, Jan 28: 7am–7pm
* Thursday, Jan 29: 12pm–7pm
📅 Election Day is this Saturday, Jan 31 (7am–7pm)
You can vote at any polling location. Find one near you and check if you live in TX-18: christianmenefee.com/vote [http://christianmenefee.com/vote]
If you live in the district, please make a plan to vote early. And if you don’t, please forward to someone who does.
I cannot overstate how important it is for us to show up in every way we can at this moment. And showing up to vote is showing up for our community and our country at a time we need it the most.
Together we can do anything,
Lizzie Signature [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/82676/images/lizzie_signature-1.png]

I am a survivor of child trafficking--and today, I work to make sure other children never face what I did. My name is Theresa Flores. **I was fifteen years old.****An honor student.
****A daughter.
****A girl who trusted the wrong "friend. "**I was trafficked for two years.Most people imagine trafficking happens far away - in dark alleys or foreign countries. **To "other people."**But my nightmare happened in the suburbs of Detroit.I lived at home.

****And to report it.** This is how **prevention becomes possible**. Because one informed employee and one brave phone call can save a life.**Here's the truth most people don 't know.**The majority of trafficking in America happens in hotels and motels.And it spikes around large sports events, conventions and concerts - anywhere demand increases. **There 's more you should know. **

* Human trafficking is the second-largest criminal enterprise in the world.
* **In the United States alone, 9 out of 10 missing children are trafficked.**
* If a child is not found within 48 hours, the risk of trafficking skyrockets.
* The average age of a trafficked child is 12 to 14 years old.

Survivors are offered opportunities to learn self-defense, engage in therapeutic art and movement, and build practical life skills.Sessions help survivors learn forgiveness, rebuild trust, form healthy relationships, and set strong boundaries.How we care for survivors matters just as much as rescuing them. You are hearing from me today because the Sound of Freedom Foundation helps make this work possible.And because children are worth fighting for.I want you to know this:Your support is not abstract. It reaches motel rooms and frightened children - in momentswhen seconds matter. It reaches places I once stood-- without help.Today, by the grace of God, I am a survivor. An advocate.And the author so others can recognize the signs sooner.But my story is not the point. The children who are still trapped are. Every outreach is a race against time. Every trained volunteer is a shield.And YOU can be part of the rescue.Whether you give once or stand with the Sound of Freedom Foundation through steady, monthly support - your generosity saves lives - quietly, consistently and courageously. YOU can help save children from harm.We would be deeply grateful.THANK YOU. You are helping rewrite endings. You are helping children believe freedom is possible. For God's Children, Theresa Flores Freedom Fighter For the Sound of Freedom Foundation 6671 Southwest Freeway, Suite 700, Houston TX 77074

clean_body: The message Charlie carried into eternity| | | | | Peter, | | Charlie Kirk built a movement for truth -- but his final message pointed to something eternal. It wasn't about politics... or elections... or even about the culture war. His final book was deeply personal, and unlike anything Charlie had written before... It was about the Sabbath. About sacred rest. Reconnecting with God. Charlie wrote this book because he knew what America was missing... and what he nearly lost himself. He found that in a world addicted to busyness, noise, and scrolling... The most radical act of resistance is to STOP. To rest. To reflect. To return to God. This book is his blueprint for how we do that -- as individuals, as families, and as a nation. 🔥 You'll discover how Charlie learned to honor the Sabbath in a culture that never stops 🔥 How setting aside just one day a week gave him clarity, peace, and strength 🔥 Why he believed this message could spark a spiritual revival across America I know he would've wanted you to have this book. When you give today to Turning Point USA, you 're not just supporting the movement Charlie built -- you're helping pass on the message he felt most urgently in his final months. Peter, thank you, in advance, for helping reach the next generation with truth, faith, and moral courage -- the very things Charlie gave his life for. And as you do, may the message of this book lead you -- just as it led Charlie -- to a deeper trust in God, a stronger love for your family, and a renewed peace in your own soul. For Charlie, Justin Streiff Chief Operating Officer Turning Point USA P.S. body:

| | Peter – The recent events in Minnesota are tragic, abhorrent, and absolutely unacceptable.

ICE has shirked accountability and transparency for too long, and the consequences are deadly. Something has to change.

Here’s what I’m doing to fight back.

Over two decades covering Latin America's turbulent intersection of politics, oil, and narcotics, the so-called "war on drugs" often masks deeper geopolitical maneuvers. The stunning events of this week--U.S. forces capturing Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro on January 3, 2026, in a swift operation [involving airstrikes and his extradition](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/869f9d29-6514-4581-abcf-51e555ba04f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to face charges in the United States--mark a pivotal chapter in this saga.

To truly grasp Maduro's downfall and Venezuela's chaos, one must delve into the entangled history involving U.S. figures like George H.W. Bush, Dick Cheney, and the Bush brothers--Jeb as Florida's governor and George W. as Texas governor and later president--and their fraught ties to the regime of Hugo Chavez, Maduro's predecessor. This narrative, steeped in the war on drugs, reveals patterns of interventionism that culminated in the policy clashes between Donald Trump and Marco Rubio, paving the way for regime change.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_._o1rTVEPU38mB7ydr1iMsYWJCLO2dcYK2bRnBHCmDxk?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=186121391)
Let's rewind to the roots. Post [Reagan and Grenada](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/1d0894b5-c5d1-4979-87fb-49045ec8f1c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - [Contras in Nicaragua](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/f84267ad-54ec-4b94-ac36-cd62d3ccf544?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Thatcher and Falklands](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/3c834ca4-f9b8-4ceb-b717-b12a7923e990?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 1980's, the George H.W. Bush's era set the stage for U.S. suspicion toward Latin American leftists. As CIA director in the 1970s, vice president under Reagan, and president from 1989 to 1993, Bush oversaw operations in the region amid the escalating [war on drugs](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/de3508fa-9bb1-41d9-972c-57e32bb6308a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), officially inaugurated by Nixon in June 1971. Bush's administration intensified efforts against Colombian cartels, but Venezuela, under presidents like Carlos Andres Perez, was seen as a cooperative ally in stemming cocaine flows northward. However, Bush's family ties to oil--through companies like Zapata Offshore--highlighted the dual U.S. interests in energy and narcotics control. Venezuela's vast reserves, [largest in world](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/abd76db5-d474-4e89-b8e5-43c42bd8b85d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), made it a strategic partner, yet corruption in its state oil company, PDVSA, already hinted at future narco-infiltration.

Dick Cheney, who served as defense secretary under H.W. Bush and later vice president under George W. Bush, embodied this oil-narcotics nexus. Cheney's Halliburton tenure intertwined with Venezuelan contracts, but his public stance turned hostile toward Chavez after the Venezuelan leader's 1999 rise to power. In a 2007 speech, Cheney lambasted Chavez for undermining democracy--[famously gaffing](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/066f995d-6489-4c95-8810-e0e2baec3fc5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by referring to Venezuela as "Peru"--while accusing him of aligning with anti-U.S. forces.
This rhetoric escalated as Venezuela became a key transit hub for drugs. By the mid-2000s, U.S. officials estimated that 200-300 tons of cocaine passed through Venezuela annually, often with alleged complicity from military officials in the "Cartel of the Suns."

Enter the Bush brothers, whose state-level roles amplified federal policies. George W. Bush, as Texas governor from 1995 to 2000, grappled with drug influxes across the southern border. Texas ports and highways were pipelines for Venezuelan-sourced narcotics, funneled via Mexican cartels. Bush's "zero tolerance" approach mirrored national efforts, but his governorship coincided with Chavez's early reforms, which included nationalizing oil assets and criticizing U.S. imperialism. When W. became president in 2001, relations soured dramatically. The 2002 coup attempt against Chavez--briefly ousting him before his reinstatement--drew accusations of U.S. involvement, though denied by the administration.

Chavez retaliated by suspending cooperation with the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) in 2005, claiming it spied on his government.
Bush countered by decertifying Venezuela as a drug-fighting partner, citing rampant corruption.

Meanwhile, Jeb Bush's governorship of Florida from 1999 to 2007 placed him at the epicenter of the drug war. Florida's coasts were prime landing spots for speedboats carrying Venezuelan cocaine, contributing to the state's overdose epidemics. Jeb pushed aggressive anti-drug initiatives, including Operation Panama Express, a federal task force targeting Caribbean routes. But his tenure overlapped with Chavez's growing defiance. Venezuela's refusal to extradite suspects and its alliances with Colombia's FARC guerrillas--labeled narco-terrorists by the U.S.--frustrated Florida officials.

Dick Cheney's Halliburton (CEO 1995-2000) had historical ties to Venezuelan oil through subsidiaries like Brown & Root, including alleged bribery for contracts in the late 1990s (pre-Chavez full nationalization). These involved potential payoffs for PDVSA work--Cheney severed ties upon becoming VP in 2001, and investigations focused on Halliburton, not the Cheney or Bushes personally.

Jeb's family legacy added layers: rumors swirled about earlier Bush connections to Latin American figures, though unsubstantiated.

Critically, the Bushes' oil interests clashed with Chavez's "Bolivarian Revolution," which redirected PDVSA profits to social programs while allegedly enabling drug lords.
Under George W. Bush's presidency, U.S.-Venezuela ties hit rock bottom. Chavez famously called Bush "[the devil](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/f1ea6607-fc95-42f6-b595-8bc2da4ae79c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" at the 2006 UN General Assembly, decrying U.S. hegemony.

Bush sharpened criticisms, accusing Chavez of provocations and failing the drug war.

Venezuela's oil exports to the U.S. continued, notoriously to blue states like Massachusetts and also the Bronx in New York City [in individual deals](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/f6ed4955-f809-4c34-8591-1f3e7d62cdee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), in defiance of the Republican administration, but sanctions loomed. Chavez saying he is leading a socialist "revolution" and has become one Bush's strongest critics in Latin America.
Cheney, as VP, advocated hawkish stances, viewing Chavez as a threat akin to Saddam Hussein. This era solidified Venezuela as a "narco-state" in U.S. eyes, with intelligence reports linking regime officials to trafficking.

Maduro, Chavez's handpicked successor after his 2013 death, inherited this animosity. By then, the war on drugs had evolved into a tool for regime pressure. Enter Donald Trump and Marco Rubio, whose policy divergences underscore the path to this week's upheaval. Trump, during his 2016 campaign, promised an end to endless interventions, criticizing Bush-era wars. Yet his first term (2017-2021) ramped up sanctions on Maduro, recognizing opposition leader Juan Guaido as interim president in 2019 and indicting Maduro on narcotrafficking charges in 2020. Trump's approach blended isolationism with targeted pressure, focusing on oil embargoes to starve the regime.

Marco Rubio, the Cuban-American senator from Florida since 2011, brought a more interventionist bent to the State Department. Elected during Jeb Bush's post-governorship influence--Jeb endorsed Rubio's 2010 Senate bid--Rubio's heritage fueled his hardline stance against leftist regimes. As chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, he championed aggressive policies, labeling Maduro a "narco-dictator" and advocating military options if needed. Rubio's differences with Trump emerged starkly: while Trump hesitated on full regime change, Rubio pushed for it, co-authoring bills to arm Venezuelan opposition and tighten sanctions.

The war on terror plays a part too. Qatar and Iran's influences in Venezuela have deepened under Maduro's regime, intertwining with drugs, terrorism, and regional instability, while exacerbating religious persecution domestically.

Qatar's role is primarily economic and diplomatic, providing investments in oil and infrastructure to bypass U.S. sanctions. Though not directly linked to drugs, Qatar has harbored figures accused of terrorism and offered Maduro potential exile amid U.S. pressures.

Its Al Jazeera network has amplified pro-Maduro narratives, indirectly supporting the regime's stability.

Iran's involvement is more insidious, bolstering Maduro through military aid, oil deals, and Hezbollah networks. Iranian-backed Hezbollah operates in Venezuela for drug trafficking, money laundering, and terrorism financing, converging with groups like FARC.

This "narcoterrorism" nexus funnels cocaine through Venezuela, impacting Colombia--where drug production fuels border conflicts--and Mexico, where Sinaloa and other cartels use Venezuelan ports for transit, escalating violence and U.S.-bound flows.

Religiously, Maduro's authoritarianism targets Christians, with hostility toward outreach, repression of church leaders advocating reform, and systemic violations of faith freedoms, potentially worsening post-capture.

Iran's Shia influence may indirectly fuel sectarian tensions, though direct ties are limited.

These alliances have turned Venezuela into a hub for illicit activities, destabilizing neighbors.

In 2019, Rubio urged Trump to invoke the [Monroe Doctrine](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/2b3bd3d6-bad1-4cce-be53-6a0325dce596?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), but Trump demurred, tweeting "all options are on the table" without committing troops.

These tensions resurfaced in Trump's second term, starting 2025. With Rubio as Secretary of State, the duo navigated a fragile alliance.

Trump, eyeing Venezuela's oil amid global shortages, authorized a military buildup in the Caribbean, framing it as anti-drug operations.

Airstrikes on alleged drug vessels escalated in late 2025, echoing Bush-era interdictions but with modern drone tech.

Rubio, the hawk, reportedly advocated for direct action, while Trump initially favored negotiations for oil access. Disagreements peaked over post-Maduro governance: Trump boasted the U.S. would "run" Venezuela to exploit its resources, coining it the "[Don-roe Doctrine](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/33eb4c0a-1f16-4bd3-bfb5-b5f03b1984d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)", while Rubio emphasized democratic transitions without occupation.

Rubio's Cuban roots and Florida ties--echoing Jeb's drug war focus--prioritized human rights and anti-communism, contrasting Trump's transactionalism.
This policy friction, rooted in the Bush-Cheney legacy of viewing Venezuela through a drugs-and-oil lens, led to the January 3 operation. Codenamed **Operation Absolute Resolve** for swift extraction, it captured Maduro amid claims of his regime's drug empire costing U.S. lives.

Critics decry it as "naked imperialism," a return to unilateral interventions.

Yet, as Maduro faces trial, Venezuela's future hangs in limbo--opposition fragmented, U.S. influence deepened.

Understanding Maduro requires this historical lens: from H.W. Bush's foundational anti-drug crusades, through Cheney's and the Bushes' confrontations with Chavez, to Trump-Rubio rifts. The war on drugs has long been a pretext for power plays, and this week's regime change proves the cycle endures. As Venezuelans awaken to uncertainty, the ghosts of U.S. policy past loom large.

_Editorial comments expressed in this column are the sole opinion of the writer._

The most damning document the U.S. government produced on Maduro before Saturday was the [2020 indictment handed up by a federal grand jury in Manhattan ](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/15d43df1-8307-460f-a4c3-2a654fce06ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)at the request of the first Trump Justice Department. The indictment chronicles how Maduro seized power after rising through the ranks of a drug cartel closely aligned with Colombia's leftist guerrillas and drug traffickers.

You can read that indictment here.
[maduro_moros_et_al_superseding_indictment_sdny_redacted_0.pdf](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/2d0e2c60-4b90-4324-989c-cb720a97de2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Since at least 1999, the indictment claimed, Maduro and his cohorts "acted as leaders and managers of the Cartel de Los Soles," also known as Cartel of the Suns.

clean_body: When the Monroe Doctrine gets a 'Don-roe' upgrade, even cartels start checking their extradition policies. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more When the Monroe Doctrine gets a 'Don-roe' upgrade, even cartels start checking their extradition policies. | | | Jan 28 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Over two decades covering Latin America's turbulent intersection of politics, oil, and narcotics, the so-called "war on drugs" often masks deeper geopolitical maneuvers. The stunning events of this week--U.S. forces capturing Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro on January 3, 2026, in a swift operation to face charges in the United States--mark a pivotal chapter in this saga. To truly grasp Maduro's downfall and Venezuela's chaos, one must delve into the entangled history involving U.S. figures like George H.W. Bush, Dick Cheney, and the Bush brothers--Jeb as Florida's governor and George W. as Texas governor and later president--and their fraught ties to the regime of Hugo Chavez, Maduro's predecessor. This narrative, steeped in the war on drugs, reveals patterns of interventionism that culminated in the policy clashes between Donald Trump and Marco Rubio, paving the way for regime change. Let's rewind to the roots. Post - , 1980's, the George H.W. Bush's era set the stage for U.S. suspicion toward Latin American leftists. As CIA director in the 1970s, vice president under Reagan, and president from 1989 to 1993, Bush oversaw operations in the region amid the escalating , officially inaugurated by Nixon in June 1971. Bush's administration intensified efforts against Colombian cartels, but Venezuela, under presidents like Carlos Andres Perez, was seen as a cooperative ally in stemming cocaine flows northward. However, Bush's family ties to oil--through companies like Zapata Offshore--highlighted the dual U.S. interests in energy and narcotics control. Venezuela's vast reserves, , made it a strategic partner, yet corruption in its state oil company, PDVSA, already hinted at future narco-infiltration. Dick Cheney, who served as defense secretary under H.W. Bush and later vice president under George W. Bush, embodied this oil-narcotics nexus. Cheney's Halliburton tenure intertwined with Venezuelan contracts, but his public stance turned hostile toward Chavez after the Venezuelan leader's 1999 rise to power. In a 2007 speech, Cheney lambasted Chavez for undermining democracy-- by referring to Venezuela as "Peru"--while accusing him of aligning with anti-U.S. forces. This rhetoric escalated as Venezuela became a key transit hub for drugs. By the mid-2000s, U.S. officials estimated that 200-300 tons of cocaine passed through Venezuela annually, often with alleged complicity from military officials in the "Cartel of the Suns." Enter the Bush brothers, whose state-level roles amplified federal policies. George W. Bush, as Texas governor from 1995 to 2000, grappled with drug influxes across the southern border. Texas ports and highways were pipelines for Venezuelan-sourced narcotics, funneled via Mexican cartels. Bush's "zero tolerance" approach mirrored national efforts, but his governorship coincided with Chavez's early reforms, which included nationalizing oil assets and criticizing U.S. imperialism. When W. became president in 2001, relations soured dramatically. The 2002 coup attempt against Chavez--briefly ousting him before his reinstatement--drew accusations of U.S. involvement, though denied by the administration. Chavez retaliated by suspending cooperation with the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) in 2005, claiming it spied on his government. Bush countered by decertifying Venezuela as a drug-fighting partner, citing rampant corruption. Meanwhile, Jeb Bush's governorship of Florida from 1999 to 2007 placed him at the epicenter of the drug war. Florida's coasts were prime landing spots for speedboats carrying Venezuelan cocaine, contributing to the state's overdose epidemics. Jeb pushed aggressive anti-drug initiatives, including Operation Panama Express, a federal task force targeting Caribbean routes. But his tenure overlapped with Chavez's growing defiance. Venezuela's refusal to extradite suspects and its alliances with Colombia's FARC guerrillas--labeled narco-terrorists by the U.S.--frustrated Florida officials. Dick Cheney's Halliburton (CEO 1995-2000) had historical ties to Venezuelan oil through subsidiaries like Brown & Root, including alleged bribery for contracts in the late 1990s (pre-Chavez full nationalization). These involved potential payoffs for PDVSA work--Cheney severed ties upon becoming VP in 2001, and investigations focused on Halliburton, not the Cheney or Bushes personally. Jeb's family legacy added layers: rumors swirled about earlier Bush connections to Latin American figures, though unsubstantiated. Critically, the Bushes' oil interests clashed with Chavez's "Bolivarian Revolution," which redirected PDVSA profits to social programs while allegedly enabling drug lords. Under George W. Bush's presidency, U.S.-Venezuela ties hit rock bottom. Chavez famously called Bush "" at the 2006 UN General Assembly, decrying U.S. hegemony. Bush sharpened criticisms, accusing Chavez of provocations and failing the drug war. Venezuela's oil exports to the U.S. continued, notoriously to blue states like Massachusetts and also the Bronx in New York City , in defiance of the Republican administration, but sanctions loomed. Chavez saying he is leading a socialist "revolution" and has become one Bush's strongest critics in Latin America. Cheney, as VP, advocated hawkish stances, viewing Chavez as a threat akin to Saddam Hussein. This era solidified Venezuela as a "narco-state" in U.S. eyes, with intelligence reports linking regime officials to trafficking. Maduro, Chavez's handpicked successor after his 2013 death, inherited this animosity. By then, the war on drugs had evolved into a tool for regime pressure. Enter Donald Trump and Marco Rubio, whose policy divergences underscore the path to this week's upheaval. Trump, during his 2016 campaign, promised an end to endless interventions, criticizing Bush-era wars. Yet his first term (2017-2021) ramped up sanctions on Maduro, recognizing opposition leader Juan Guaido as interim president in 2019 and indicting Maduro on narcotrafficking charges in 2020. Trump's approach blended isolationism with targeted pressure, focusing on oil embargoes to starve the regime. Marco Rubio, the Cuban-American senator from Florida since 2011, brought a more interventionist bent to the State Department. Elected during Jeb Bush's post-governorship influence--Jeb endorsed Rubio's 2010 Senate bid--Rubio's heritage fueled his hardline stance against leftist regimes. As chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, he championed aggressive policies, labeling Maduro a "narco-dictator" and advocating military options if needed. Rubio's differences with Trump emerged starkly: while Trump hesitated on full regime change, Rubio pushed for it, co-authoring bills to arm Venezuelan opposition and tighten sanctions. The war on terror plays a part too. Qatar and Iran's influences in Venezuela have deepened under Maduro's regime, intertwining with drugs, terrorism, and regional instability, while exacerbating religious persecution domestically. Qatar's role is primarily economic and diplomatic, providing investments in oil and infrastructure to bypass U.S. sanctions. Though not directly linked to drugs, Qatar has harbored figures accused of terrorism and offered Maduro potential exile amid U.S. pressures. Its Al Jazeera network has amplified pro-Maduro narratives, indirectly supporting the regime's stability. Iran's involvement is more insidious, bolstering Maduro through military aid, oil deals, and Hezbollah networks. Iranian-backed Hezbollah operates in Venezuela for drug trafficking, money laundering, and terrorism financing, converging with groups like FARC. This "narcoterrorism" nexus funnels cocaine through Venezuela, impacting Colombia--where drug production fuels border conflicts--and Mexico, where Sinaloa and other cartels use Venezuelan ports for transit, escalating violence and U.S.-bound flows. Religiously, Maduro's authoritarianism targets Christians, with hostility toward outreach, repression of church leaders advocating reform, and systemic violations of faith freedoms, potentially worsening post-capture. Iran's Shia influence may indirectly fuel sectarian tensions, though direct ties are limited. These alliances have turned Venezuela into a hub for illicit activities, destabilizing neighbors. In 2019, Rubio urged Trump to invoke the , but Trump demurred, tweeting "all options are on the table" without committing troops. These tensions resurfaced in Trump's second term, starting 2025. With Rubio as Secretary of State, the duo navigated a fragile alliance. Trump, eyeing Venezuela's oil amid global shortages, authorized a military buildup in the Caribbean, framing it as anti-drug operations. Airstrikes on alleged drug vessels escalated in late 2025, echoing Bush-era interdictions but with modern drone tech. Rubio, the hawk, reportedly advocated for direct action, while Trump initially favored negotiations for oil access. Disagreements peaked over post-Maduro governance: Trump boasted the U.S. would "run" Venezuela to exploit its resources, coining it the "", while Rubio emphasized democratic transitions without occupation. Rubio's Cuban roots and Florida ties--echoing Jeb's drug war focus--prioritized human rights and anti-communism, contrasting Trump's transactionalism. This policy friction, rooted in the Bush-Cheney legacy of viewing Venezuela through a drugs-and-oil lens, led to the January 3 operation. Codenamed Operation Absolute Resolve for swift extraction, it captured Maduro amid claims of his regime's drug empire costing U.S. lives. Critics decry it as "naked imperialism," a return to unilateral interventions. Yet, as Maduro faces trial, Venezuela's future hangs in limbo--opposition fragmented, U.S. influence deepened. Understanding Maduro requires this historical lens: from H.W. Bush's foundational anti-drug crusades, through Cheney's and the Bushes' confrontations with Chavez, to Trump-Rubio rifts. The war on drugs has long been a pretext for power plays, and this week's regime change proves the cycle endures. As Venezuelans awaken to uncertainty, the ghosts of U.S. policy past loom large. Editorial comments expressed in this column are the sole opinion of the writer. The most damning document the U.S. government produced on Maduro before Saturday was the the request of the first Trump Justice Department. The indictment chronicles how Maduro seized power after rising through the ranks of a drug cartel closely aligned with Colombia's leftist guerrillas and drug traffickers. You can read that indictment here. Since at least 1999, the indictment claimed, Maduro and his cohorts "acted as leaders and managers of the Cartel de Los Soles," also known as Cartel of the Suns. # Nurse who suggested paralyzing ICE agents fired
A Virginia Commonwealth University Health nurse was **[swiftly fired after posting TikTok videos](https://substack.com/redirect/ed10a41e-64ac-477b-a7db-49a05735ff70?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** urging medical professionals to sabotage ICE agents by injecting them with paralytic drugs like succinylcholine or slipping laxatives into their drinks, amid outrage over the fatal shooting of another nurse by ICE in Minneapolis.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ed10a41e-64ac-477b-a7db-49a05735ff70?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Hospital Launches Swift Probe** VCU Health suspended then terminated Malinda Rose Cook following an internal investigation into her inflammatory social media posts, also reporting her to local law enforcement under Virginia state law for potential violations.
* **Videos Detail Sabotage Tactics** Cook advised using syringes filled with saline or succinylcholine to paralyze agents' muscles, poison ivy water in squirt guns for skin irritation, and ex-lax in drinks to incapacitate without killing, framing them as deniable deterrents.
* **Backlash Ties to ICE Shooting** The posts surfaced amid national protests over the January 2025 death of ICU nurse Alex Pretti, shot by an ICE officer in Minneapolis while filming demonstrations, fueling broader debates on immigration enforcement and officer accountability.

* * *
# Viral "bananas and rice" Somali woman arrested obstructing ICE
A Somali-American woman **[famous for her viral"bananas and rice"](https://substack.com/redirect/01b92df5-a6b0-42f0-abfa-f02a6bcd172d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** cultural speech was arrested Wednesday in Minnesota for allegedly obstructing federal officers during heated anti-ICE protests, U.S. Attorney General Pam Bondi announced.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/01b92df5-a6b0-42f0-abfa-f02a6bcd172d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Viral Speech Sparks Recognition** Nasra Ahmed gained fame from a widely shared clip explaining Somali identity as a "cultural fusion" of bananas and rice, which resurfaced prominently after her arrest tied her to the ongoing unrest.
* **Federal Crackdown Targets Protesters** Attorney General Pam Bondi, on the ground with agents, revealed 16 arrests including Ahmed for impeding operations amid attacks on hotels believed to house ICE personnel.
* **Arrests Follow Deadly Incidents** The federal action follows fatal shootings of Renee Good and Alex Pretti during enforcement operations, escalating tensions in Minnesota's anti-ICE demonstrations that led to the obstruction charges.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4d5cc54a-f801-46c9-9264-818f042b5577?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
